<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the sharp Penrose inequality for three-dimensional maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data with spherical conformal infinity. Under the dominant energy condition, the stated decay and integrability assumptions, and a future-timelike mass covector, the invariant mass is bounded below by the Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter mass associated with the minimum enclosing area of a weakly future outer-trapped boundary. The boundary may be disconnected, and no restriction is imposed on the compact topology.

- **claim-maximal-penrose** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): Under <a href="#eq:decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:decay">[eq:decay]</a>–<a href="#eq:future-trapping" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:future-trapping">[eq:future-trapping]</a>, the completeness, one-end, and smoothness assumptions above, and the future-timelike condition <a href="#eq:invariant-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:invariant-mass">[eq:invariant-mass]</a>, one has $$\label{eq:main-inequality} m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g)\ge\frac12\bigl(r_A+r_A^3\bigr), \qquad r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}}.$$ The coefficient is sharp: equality holds for every positive-mass time-symmetric Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter exterior bounded by its minimal horizon.
  - Explanation: The invariant mass bounds the Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter mass associated with the minimum enclosing area. The stated equality examples establish sharpness without an equality classification.
- **claim-time-component-penrose** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-ts)): Let $(\Omega,g)$ have the smoothness, topology, completeness, and end structure above. Suppose $g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_\tau$, $3/2<\tau<3$, the four fluxes <a href="#eq:ah-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-mass">[eq:ah-mass]</a> are finite, and $$R_g\ge-6,\qquad H_g(S)\le0, \qquad \int_{\mathrm{end}}V_0(R_g+6)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty.$$ In every such fixed end chart, $$\label{eq:ts-inequality} p_0(g)\ge\frac12(a+a^3), \qquad a=\sqrt{A_{\min}(S;g)/(4\pi)}.$$
  - Explanation: The time component satisfies the enclosing-area bound in every designated end chart, without assuming a causal character for the mass covector.
- **claim-compact-truncations-caps** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-core)): The sufficiently large coordinate spheres bound connected compact truncations of $\Omega$. Each component of $S$ can be capped on its other side to produce a smooth complete connected one-ended manifold $X$ without boundary, with the orientation extending that of $\Omega$. Let $O$ denote the compact cap set, including its boundary. For competitors containing $O$, perimeter depends only on the metric on $\Omega$ and its boundary trace.
  - Explanation: The end admits connected compact truncations, and orientable caps provide a boundaryless ambient manifold for enclosure minimization.
- **claim-cut-enclosure-correspondence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-cut-enclosure)): Every admissible cut from Definition <a href="#def:minimum-area" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:minimum-area">1</a> determines a precompact finite-perimeter enclosure of $O$ whose perimeter is at most the area of that cut. Conversely, a precompact enclosure of $O$ with smooth free boundary in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$ and connected exterior gives an admissible cut with the same area. If this enclosure is outward minimizing, its boundary realizes the minimum enclosing area of its own closed exterior.
  - Explanation: Admissible intrinsic cuts produce finite-perimeter enclosures; smooth free enclosures with connected exterior give converse cuts. Outward minimization identifies the new exterior's minimum enclosing area.
- **claim-lorentz-mass-covariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-mass-covariance)): Suppose $g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_\tau$, $\tau>3/2$, and $\int V_0\|R_g+6\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty$ on the end. The fluxes <a href="#eq:ah-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-mass">[eq:ah-mass]</a> transform as a Lorentz covector under hyperbolic isometries of the asymptotic chart. Such chart changes preserve the weighted decay and integrability hypotheses used here. Consequently a future-timelike original covector admits a chart with $p_0=m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}$ and $p_1=p_2=p_3=0$.
  - Explanation: Hyperbolic chart isometries preserve the analytic hypotheses and transform the mass fluxes covariantly, permitting a rest chart for the original future-timelike covector.
- **claim-af-penrose** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-af-penrose)): Let $(Y,h)$ be a complete connected one-ended three-dimensional AF manifold with smooth compact outer-minimizing minimal boundary. Assume $R_h\ge0$, $h-\delta=O_2(\|y\|^{-\beta})$ for some $\beta>1/2$, and $R_h=O(\|y\|^{-q})$ for some $q>3$. If the total boundary area is $A$, then $$\label{eq:af-penrose} m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h)\ge\sqrt{A/(16\pi)}.$$ Disconnected boundary is allowed.
  - Explanation: The asymptotically flat comparison theorem bounds mass using total outer-minimizing minimal boundary area, allowing disconnected boundary.
- **claim-scalar-elliptic-inputs** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-elliptic-inputs)): On fixed coordinate balls in dimension three the following estimates hold, with constants depending on the indicated ellipticity, coefficient, and geometry bounds.* 1. *Bounded measurable uniformly elliptic divergence matrices admit local subsolution bounds, weak Harnack estimates for nonnegative supersolutions, and inhomogeneous Harnack and Hölder estimates for nonnegative solutions. Bounded divergence drifts multiplying the unknown, vector forcing in $L^q$, $q>3$, and scalar forcing in $L^p$, $p>3/2$, are permitted in the corresponding estimates.* 2. *For Laplace equations with uniformly positive Lipschitz metric coefficients in interior or flattened smooth boundary charts, divergence forcing in $L^q$ gives local $W^{1,q}$ estimates. Scalar forcing in $L^2$ can be included for $3<q<6$. The same statements hold with local zero Dirichlet data or natural Neumann data, with the divergence forcing included in the conormal current. A boundary datum in $L^{p_1}$, $p_1>2$, permits a choice $3<q<3p_1/2$ sufficiently close to $3$.* 3. *Smooth-coefficient scalar Dirichlet and conormal problems have the usual Schauder estimates, including divergence-form $C^{1,\gamma}$ estimates when the uniformly elliptic coefficients and vector forcing are $C^\gamma$, with boundary data of the corresponding regularity. These estimates are used only after their coefficient hypotheses have been obtained.* 4. *For a bounded measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix $a$ on a ball, its positive Dirichlet Green kernel is bounded above by $C\|z-z'\|^{-1}$, and below by $c\|z-z'\|^{-1}$ when the pole and the nearby evaluation point lie in a fixed smaller ball.
  - Explanation: Local scalar divergence, Laplace, Schauder, and Green-kernel estimates are available under their separately stated coefficient and forcing conditions. These inputs alone do not establish nonlinear transmission regularity.
- **claim-static-graph-curvature** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-graph-curvature)): Suppose that $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p=TN$, where $T$ is a smooth scalar function. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\pi=T$ and $$\begin{aligned} \bar\nabla\log s&=\nabla\log N-\pi(v), \label{eq:calculus-lapse-differential}\\ R_{\bar g} &=R_g+T^2-\|\pi\|^2-2(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\pi-\mathop{}\!\mathrm dT)\cdot v. \label{eq:calculus-static-curvature} \end{aligned}$$ More generally, let $\mathcal K$ be any smooth symmetric covariant tensor, and define $$\kappa=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\mathcal K,\qquad \ell=T-\kappa,\qquad \lambda=\pi-\mathcal K, \qquad C=\lambda-\ell g, \label{eq:calculus-trace-definitions}$$ and $$\mathscr D(v)=R_g+\kappa^2-\|\mathcal K\|^2 -2(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal K-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\kappa)\cdot v. \label{eq:calculus-dominant-expression}$$ Then $$R_{\bar g}=\mathscr D(v)+\|\lambda\|^2-\ell^2 -\frac2N\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp). \label{eq:calculus-completed-curvature}$$
  - Explanation: The graph curvature identity separates the dominant expression, tensor difference terms, and a divergence current.
- **claim-graph-current-conformal-curvature** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-graph-current)): Under the hypotheses and notation of Lemma <a href="#lem:graph-curvature" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:graph-curvature">9</a>, set $$B=\nabla N-(\mathcal K+\ell g)p,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B=\Phi,\qquad -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)=\Psi, \qquad Q=B+A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw. \label{eq:calculus-general-system}$$ Then $$\begin{aligned} Q&=N\bar\nabla x+xCp-(x-1)B,\notag\\ \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g Q&=\Phi-\Psi, \label{eq:calculus-general-current}\\ N\Delta_{\bar g}x+x\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp)&=x\Phi-\Psi, \label{eq:calculus-general-x}\\ xR_h&=\mathscr D(v)+\|\lambda\|^2-\ell^2 -\frac{2\Phi}{N}+\frac{2\Psi}{Nx} +\frac32\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log x\|_{\bar g}^2. \label{eq:calculus-general-conformal} \end{aligned}$$ In particular, the following two specializations hold.* **The maximal AH system.* If $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0$ and $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p=0,\quad B=\nabla N-Kp,\quad \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B=3N+\Sigma,\quad -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)=3N+\Sigma x+P, \label{eq:calculus-ah-system}$$ then, writing $D=R_g+6-\|K\|^2-2\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gK\cdot v$, one has $$\begin{aligned} Q&=N\bar\nabla x+x(\pi-K)p-(x-1)B,\notag\\ \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g Q&=-(x-1)\Sigma-P, \label{eq:calculus-ah-current}\\ \left(\Delta_{\bar g}-3+ N^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g((\pi-K)p)\right)x&=-3-P/N, \label{eq:calculus-ah-x}\\ x^2(R_h+6) &=x\bigl(D+\|\pi-K\|^2\bigr) +\frac{3}{2x}\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx\|_{\bar g}^2 +6(x-1)^2+\frac{2P}{N}. \label{eq:calculus-ah-curvature} \end{aligned}$$ For the constraint densities in <a href="#eq:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:constraints">[eq:constraints]</a>, $D=16\pi(\mu-J\cdot v)\ge0$ under the dominant energy condition.* **The compact trace system.* Let $0\le u_*\le1$ be constant and take $\mathcal K=u_*K$, $\kappa=u_*\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$, $\ell=T-\kappa$. If $$\begin{aligned} \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p&=TN,& B&=\nabla N-(u_*K+\ell g)p,\\ \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B&=\Sigma_++\Sigma_-,& -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)&=\Sigma_+x+P, \end{aligned} \label{eq:calculus-compact-system}$$ then $$\begin{aligned} Q&=N\bar\nabla x+x(\lambda-\ell g)p-(x-1)B,\notag\\ \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gQ&=-(x-1)\Sigma_+-P+\Sigma_-, \label{eq:calculus-compact-current}\\ xR_h&=\mathscr D(v)+\|\lambda\|^2-\ell^2 -\frac{2\Sigma_-}{N}+\frac{2P}{Nx} +\frac32\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log x\|_{\bar g}^2. \label{eq:calculus-compact-curvature} \end{aligned}$$ Here $\lambda=\pi-u_*K$. At $u_*=1$ this is the scalar identity for the synthetic data. It also holds on the outer region with $p=T=K=\ell=0$, $\Sigma_-=0$, and $\mathscr D=R_{g_o}$.
  - Explanation: The lapse and conformal equations yield exact current and scalar-curvature identities, with separate maximal hyperbolic and compact trace specializations.
- **claim-constant-height-boundary** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-graph-boundary)): Let $\mathcal S$ be a smooth two-sided hypersurface on which $f$ is constant. Choose a $g$-unit normal $n$, and write $H=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{\mathcal S}n$, $\hat z=v\cdot n$, $y=\hat z^2$, and $k_T=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{\mathcal S}\mathcal K$. The same directed normal is used on each side if $\mathcal S$ is a gluing face. Then $$\begin{aligned} d^2\partial_n\log s&=B_n/N-k_T\hat z+yH, \label{eq:calculus-boundary-lapse}\\ s\sqrt{x}\,H_h &=N(H-k_T\hat z)+B_n+(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)_n/x. \label{eq:calculus-boundary} \end{aligned}$$ In particular, in the maximal AH system with $v=-z n$, $k=K(n,n)$, $B_n=-b_S$, and $(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)_n=0$, $$s\sqrt{x}\,H_h=N(H-zk)-b_S=NH+\partial_nN. \label{eq:calculus-ah-boundary}$$ In the compact system, if $H\le0$, $k_T<0$, $\hat z\le0$, $B_n=-b_*<0$, and $(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)_n=0$, then $H_h<0$.* *Suppose, at a compact gluing face, that $N_o=s_i$, that $w$ and the normal fluxes of $B,A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw$ agree, that $f$ is constant on the inner face, and that $p=0$ outside. The induced $h$-metrics then agree. If the inner base mean curvature satisfies $H_i>\|k_T\|$ and the outer one is $H_o=\sqrt{H_i^2-k_T^2}$, then $H_{h,i}\ge H_{h,o}$, both measured toward the end.
  - Explanation: Constant height makes boundary curvature expressible through directed normal fluxes. Compatible gluing data produce matching induced metrics and the required mean-curvature ordering.
- **claim-gradient-maximum** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-gradient-maximum)): Let $N>0,f,\mathcal K,T$ be smooth and satisfy $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p=TN$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g[\nabla N-(\mathcal K+\ell g)p]=\Phi$, with the definitions above. Suppose on the region in question that $$\|\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g\|+\|\mathcal K\|+ \|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal K-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\mathcal K\|+\|T\|\le C_0, \qquad \Phi\le C_0N+\Sigma,\qquad \Sigma\ge0. \label{eq:calculus-maximum-hypotheses}$$ At a point where $m=\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\|>0$, set $$\begin{aligned} l&=\log m,\quad u=\log N,\quad e=\nabla f/m,\quad y=\|v\|^2,\\ q&=\frac{1-y}{1+y},\quad \beta=1+q,\quad \mathcal P=g^{-1}+(q-1)e\otimes e,\quad G=-\log s. \end{aligned} \label{eq:calculus-gradient-notation}$$ Let $j$ be twice continuously differentiable with $j''>0$, with either sign allowed for $j'$, and let $\eta$ be a twice continuously differentiable localization function. At an interior local maximum of $G+j(f)+\eta$ with $y\ge1/2$, $$j''q m^2\le C\left[1+\frac\Sigma N +(1-y)^2(j'm)^2+\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\eta\|^2+\|\nabla^2\eta\|\right], \label{eq:calculus-gradient-maximum}$$ where $C$ depends only on $C_0$. In particular, at that point, $$W^2\le\frac C{j''}\left[ N^2+N\Sigma+(j')^2 +N^2\bigl(\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\eta\|^2+\|\nabla^2\eta\|\bigr)\right]. \label{eq:calculus-gradient-weighted}$$ No positive lower bound for $N$, no derivative bound for $T$, and no second derivative bound for $N$ enter these two estimates.* *At a constant-height boundary, with the notation of Lemma <a href="#lem:graph-boundary" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:graph-boundary">11</a>, the exact normal derivative is $$d^2\partial_n\bigl(G+j(f)+\eta\bigr) =-B_n/N+k_T\hat z-yH+j'\hat z/N+d^2\partial_n\eta. \label{eq:calculus-gradient-boundary}$$ For the maximal AH inner boundary, if $H\le k$, $b_S\ge0$, and $v=-zn$, this implies $$G_n=-\frac{yH+u_n}{1-y} =\frac{b_S/N+zk-z^2H}{1-z^2} \ge\frac{zk}{1+z}. \label{eq:calculus-ah-gradient-boundary}$$
  - Explanation: A localized maximum argument controls graph tilt without a lapse floor, a derivative bound for the trace target, or a second derivative bound for the lapse.
- **claim-gradient-energy** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-gradient-energy)): Assume the two differential equations and the geometric coefficient bounds of Lemma <a href="#lem:gradient-maximum" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:gradient-maximum">12</a>. On a region suppose, in addition, that $N,s$ have positive lower bounds and finite upper bounds, that $\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\|$ has a finite upper bound, and that $\Phi/N$ is bounded above. Constants in this Lemma may depend on these finite bounds. With $E_i=\|\nabla N\|^2+\|\nabla^2f\|^2$ and $\rho=(1+y)/d$, one has $$\mathcal P:\nabla^2G\ge cE_i-C(1+\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dG\|^2). \label{eq:calculus-energy-nondivergence}$$ There is a finite $k_0>0$, depending only on the stated bounds, such that for $Y=s^{-k_0}$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(\rho\mathcal P\mathop{}\!\mathrm dY)\ge cE_i-C. \label{eq:calculus-energy-divergence}$$ These inequalities hold also at $\mathop{}\!\mathrm df=0$, and their constants use no derivatives of $T$.* *On a region where $p=0$, $s=N$, and $\Delta N=\Phi$, the corresponding inequality is $\Delta Y\ge c\|\nabla N\|^2-C$. At a constant-height gluing face satisfying $N_o=s_i$ and matching flux of $B$, the directed inner flux $(\rho\mathcal P\mathop{}\!\mathrm dY)_n$ and outer flux $\partial_nY$ differ by a bounded amount. The bound depends only on the finite field bounds and the fixed face geometry.
  - Explanation: Finite positive lapse and scale bounds and a finite slope bound turn the differential graph identities into coercive energy inequalities, including controlled seam flux error.
- **claim-newton-flux-freezing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-newton-flux)): In the setting of Lemma <a href="#lem:gradient-energy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:gradient-energy">13</a>, let $\mathcal T_f=\nabla^2f-(\Delta f)g$. The exact smooth vector identity is $$\rho\mathcal P\nabla G =-\frac{\nabla N}{s} +\mathcal T_f\left(\frac{s^3}{N}\nabla f\right) +Ts\nabla f, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal T_f=\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(\nabla f,\cdot). \label{eq:calculus-newton}$$ The coefficient of $\mathcal T_f$ is smooth at $\mathop{}\!\mathrm df=0$.* *More specifically, in a fixed smooth face chart take compatible reference fields $\mathcal V_*=(n_*,a_*\mathop{}\!\mathrm dt,s_*)$ for $\mathcal V=(N_i,\mathop{}\!\mathrm df,N_o)$, where $t$ is inner signed unit normal distance, $n_*>0$, and $s_*=s(n_*,\|a_*\|)$. Assume the reference ranges and the actual fields lie in a fixed bounded positive lapse and finite slope range. Put $Y_*=s_*^{-k_0}$ and $$c_*=(k_0Y_*/s_*) ,\qquad \mathfrak b_*=k_0Y_*\frac{s_*^3}{n_*}a_*\nabla t.$$ For the following assertion assume also that $\Phi$ is bounded on each side. Modify the inner and outer energy fluxes by $$\mathcal J_i=\rho\mathcal P\mathop{}\!\mathrm dY+c_*B-\mathcal T_f\mathfrak b_* , \qquad \mathcal J_o=\nabla Y+c_*B. \label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux}$$ They have bounded directed flux difference across the face, and $$\begin{aligned} \|\mathcal J\|&\le C\bigl(1+\|\mathcal V-\mathcal V_*\|\sqrt E\bigr), \label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux-size}\\ \mathop{\mathrm{div}}\mathcal J&\ge c'E-C-C\delta_{\mathcal C} \label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux-divergence} \end{aligned}$$ in the joined weak formulation, with $E=E_i$ inside and $E=\|\nabla N_o\|^2$ outside. The second line is understood with the smooth metric densities in coordinates, and $\delta_{\mathcal C}$ is surface measure on the face. The same conclusion holds on an interior chart with an arbitrary constant covector reference and no face term; its metric-dependent reference coefficients are taken as smooth functions of position.
  - Explanation: An exact Newton-tensor identity permits cancellation at a compatible reference state. The modified current controls energy while its size measures departure from that state.
- **claim-flow-initial-adjustment** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-flow-initial-adjustment)): Let $\widehat h$ be a smooth complete metric on $X$, and suppose $E_0$ has the properties just described. If $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\widehat h}\ge-C_R$ on $X\setminus E_0$, then an arbitrarily small, compactly supported smooth conformal change gives a metric $\widetilde h$ for which $$\label{eq:flow-initial-adjustment} \|\partial E_0\|_{\widetilde h}=\|\partial E_0\|_{\widehat h},\qquad H_{\widetilde h}>0,\qquad \int_{\partial E_0}H_{\widetilde h}^{2}\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{\widetilde h}\le1, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\widetilde h}\ge-C_R-1 \quad\hbox{on }X\setminus E_0.$$ The set $E_0$ remains strictly outward minimizing. The size of the change may be chosen separately for every comparison metric.
  - Explanation: A small conformal collar change preserves initial area and strict outward minimization while making the initial mean curvature positive and controlling scalar curvature.
- **claim-flow-topology-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-hull-components)): At almost every positive time, every component of $E_t$ meets $E_0$, the open exterior of $E_t$ is connected, and $$\label{eq:flow-component-bound} b_0(N_t)\le b_2,\qquad \chi(N_t)\le2b_2,$$ where $b_2$ is the fixed number in <a href="#eq:flow-topology-constant" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:flow-topology-constant">[eq:flow-topology-constant]</a>.
  - Explanation: Weak-flow components remain attached to the initial enclosure, the exterior stays connected, and fixed homology bounds boundary components and Euler characteristic.
- **claim-flow-curvature-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-flow-curvature)): Suppose the adjusted metric satisfies $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\widetilde h}\ge-C_0$ outside $E_0$, and let $A_*>0$. At almost every time for which $A(t)\le A_*$, $$\label{eq:flow-uniform-curvature} J(t):=\int_{N_t}\|\nabla u\|^2\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{\widetilde h} \le C_H:=1+\frac23 C_0 A_*+16\pi b_2.$$ In particular this bound is independent of $A(0)$, even if the initial areas tend to zero in a family.
  - Explanation: The scalar lower bound and fixed topology control the squared-mean-curvature integral up to a prescribed area, independently of degeneration of the initial area.
- **claim-enclosing-area-projection** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-area-projection)): Let $N$ be a compact embedded $C^1$ enclosure of $O$, disjoint from $S$, with connected exterior.* 1. *On the original $\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}$ exterior, fix a large radius $r_p$ and put $$\label{eq:flow-ah-weight} \rho=\min\{1,r_p^2/r^2\},$$ with $\rho=1$ on the compact part. There is $q(r_p)\downarrow0$, depending only on the original end metric, such that $$\label{eq:flow-ah-projection} \int_N\rho\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_g\ge(1-q(r_p))A_*.$$* 2. *Suppose the $\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}$ extension has the parallel-surface form $g_o=U^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm dt^2+\gamma_t$, where $\gamma_t$ is induced on outward Euclidean parallels of a strictly convex embedding of $(\mathcal C,\gamma_0)$. Then, with $\rho=1$, $$\label{eq:flow-af-projection} \int_N\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{g_{\mathrm{base}}}\ge A_*.$$ For a surface crossing the joining sphere, the assertion holds for the piecewise area; it is enough that its intersection with the joining sphere have zero two-dimensional measure. In particular this holds for almost every weak-flow level.
  - Explanation: Radial projection gives weighted area control on the hyperbolic end. Projection along convex Euclidean parallels gives the corresponding comparison on the attached flat end.
- **claim-uniform-area-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-area-transfer)): Fix the capped topology $(X,O)$, a number $A_*>0$, and a scalar lower bound $C_R\ge0$. Suppose a comparison has the following properties.* 1. *The smooth complete metric $\widehat h$ has one $\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}$ or $\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}$ end with the mean-curvature and radial-gradient asymptotics used in <a href="#eq:flow-end-subsolution" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:flow-end-subsolution">[eq:flow-end-subsolution]</a>. The cap-only enclosure $E_0$ is a smooth precompact strictly outward-minimizing set, with minimal boundary disjoint from $O$, every component meeting $O$, and $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{\widehat h}\ge-C_R$ outside $E_0$.* 2. *On $X\setminus O$ there are a reference metric $g_{\mathrm{base}}$, positive functions $x,W$, a metric $\bar g$, and a weight $0<\rho\le1$, such that $$\label{eq:flow-metric-comparison} \bar g\ge g_{\mathrm{base}},\qquad \mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\bar g}=W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{g_{\mathrm{base}}},\qquad (1-\eta)x\bar g\le\widehat h\le(1+\eta)x\bar g.$$* 3. *Every enclosing $C^1$ surface with connected exterior, as in Lemma <a href="#lem:area-projection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:area-projection">18</a>, satisfies $$\label{eq:flow-abstract-projection} \int_N\rho\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{g_{\mathrm{base}}}\ge(1-q)A_*.$$ In the piecewise case this is required for surfaces having zero area in the joining surface.* *For every $0<\varepsilon<1$ there are positive tolerances $\eta_0,q_0,\delta_0$ and $v_0$, depending only on $\varepsilon,A_*,C_R$ and the integer $b_2$ in <a href="#eq:flow-topology-constant" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:flow-topology-constant">[eq:flow-topology-constant]</a>, with the following consequence. If $\eta\le\eta_0$, $q\le q_0$, $0<\delta\le\delta_0$, and $$\label{eq:flow-bad-volume} \int_{\{x<1-\delta\}}\rho^{3/2}W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{g_{\mathrm{base}}}<v_0,$$ then $$\label{eq:flow-area-conclusion} \|\partial E_0\|_{\widehat h}\ge(1-\varepsilon)A_*.$$ The tolerances are uniform over all comparisons satisfying these conditions; the geometry and initial area of $E_0$ may vary.
  - Explanation: A small weighted volume of metric contraction preserves the cap-only minimizing boundary area, provided scalar curvature, projection, topology, and metric comparisons satisfy the stated conditions.
- **claim-maximal-reduction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thm-ah-reduction)): Let $F:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and nondecreasing. Suppose that every smooth, complete, connected, orientable, one-ended asymptotically hyperbolic three-dimensional exterior with nonempty compact minimal boundary, scalar curvature at least $-6$, $g-b\in C^{2,\gamma}_\tau$ for some $0<\gamma<1$ and $3/2<\tau<3$, the weighted scalar integrability of Section <a href="#sec:hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:hypotheses">1</a>, and four finite mass fluxes satisfies $$p_0\ge F(A_{\min}).$$ The exponent $\gamma$ may depend on the comparison metric. This hypothesis is to hold in every designated asymptotic chart, without a causal-character assumption on the mass covector. Then every maximal initial-data exterior of Section <a href="#sec:hypotheses" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:hypotheses">1</a> satisfies, in each designated chart, $$p_0(g)\ge F\bigl(A_{\min}(S;g)\bigr).$$
  - Explanation: A continuous nondecreasing time-component bound for all eligible minimal-boundary Riemannian comparisons transfers to maximal initial data in each designated chart.
- **claim-ah-lapse-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-lapse)): For smooth solutions on sufficiently large truncations, uniformly over $0\le t\le1$ and $b_S\in\mathcal B_M$, $$\label{eq:ah-lapse-bounds} N\le Cr,\qquad N\ge c(M)\epsilon r,\qquad \frac{\|N-V_0\|}{r}\le C(R_s/r)^{1+\kappa}\quad(r\ge2R_s),$$ where $0<\kappa<\tau-1$ is fixed and small. The upper constant uses only the $L^{p_1}$ bound of $b_S$. On compact sets, $N$ has uniform Hölder and $W^{1,q}$ bounds for some $q>3$, depending on $M,L$, but independent of $\epsilon,d_*$ and derivatives of $b_S$.* *The positivity and lower bound remain true at a fixed point in which the drift $Z=K(v)$ is computed using a smooth positive extension of the constitutive lapse argument, provided that the actual lapse equation is $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(\nabla N-ZN)=3N+\Sigma$ and the cutoff $N\le\epsilon$ uses the actual lapse.
  - Explanation: Bounded drift suffices for lapse positivity, growth, end comparison, and compact regularity, with the specified independence from penalty strengths and boundary-data derivatives.
- **claim-ah-graph-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-graph-estimates)): The solutions satisfy $0\le f\le tM$. On every fixed compact subset, including $S$, $$\label{eq:ah-s-floor} s\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}(M,L)\epsilon ,$$ and their height gradients have finite bounds for fixed $M,L,\epsilon$, independent of $d_*$, $R$, and derivatives of $b_S$. Moreover, $$\begin{aligned} \int_{\{f\in I\}}p\cdot df&\le C\|I\|,\qquad \int_{\Omega_R}(W^2-1)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g\le CM,\label{eq:ah-height-energy}\\ \|f\|&\le C R_s^{-1}(R_s/r)^{4-\xi},\nonumber\\ \|v\|+\|\pi\|+\|\nabla\pi\|&\le C(R_s/r)^{3-\xi} \quad(r\ge C_0R_s),\label{eq:ah-end-graph} \end{aligned}$$ where $I$ is any height interval, $\xi>0$ can be fixed sufficiently small, and the constants in <a href="#eq:ah-height-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-height-energy">[eq:ah-height-energy]</a>–<a href="#eq:ah-end-graph" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-end-graph">[eq:ah-end-graph]</a> are independent of $M,L,\epsilon,d_*$ for large $M$. The end estimates include the corresponding local Hölder control and derivatives of $v$ through order two.
  - Explanation: Height maximum principles, finite-slope estimates, energy testing, and end barriers control the graph fields with the stated parameter dependence.
- **claim-ah-finite-penalties** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-penalties)): The parameters can be chosen in the order already specified, with $\epsilon$ sufficiently small after $M,L$, and then $d_*$ sufficiently large but finite, such that $$\label{eq:ah-penalty-costs} \int_{\Omega_R}P_1\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g\le C T/M,\qquad \int_{\Omega_R}P_2\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g=o_{M,L}(1) \quad(\epsilon\downarrow0),$$ uniformly in $R,b_S$, and in the strengths. At $t=1$, the same choices enforce $$\label{eq:ah-penalty-targets} w\|_S\ge T,\qquad w\ge T_2\quad\hbox{on }\{N\le2\epsilon\},\qquad sT_2\ge1\quad\hbox{on }\{N\le4\epsilon\}.$$ Consequently $x<1-\delta$ and $r\le R_s$ imply $\Sigma=L$.
  - Explanation: Successive finite penalty choices enforce boundary and low-lapse targets while their integrated mass costs become small.
- **claim-ah-limit-mass-budget** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-limit-mass)): With internal parameters fixed, the fields $N,f,df,w$ are uniformly precompact in local uniform topology, including at $S$. Limit solutions have $N,w>0$ and are classical away from $S$. They obey $$\label{eq:ah-conformal-decay} x-1=O_{\mathrm{fixed},2,\gamma}(r^{-3+\xi}).$$ Here $\xi$ is taken sufficiently small, in particular $0<\xi<\min(3-\tau,\tau-1)$. Their metrics $h$ satisfy the required asymptotically hyperbolic decay, all four mass fluxes are finite, and $V_0(\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_h+6)$ is integrable near infinity. Their time components satisfy $$\label{eq:ah-mass-budget} 8\pi\{p_0(h)-p_0(g)\} =t\int_S b_S\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_g +\int_\Omega\{(x-1)\Sigma+P\}\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g \le o(1)\quad(M\to\infty).$$ The $o(1)$ is uniform over the allowed data, with the subsequent choices of $\epsilon,d_*$ just described.
  - Explanation: Fixed-parameter compactness produces admissible limit metrics and finite mass fluxes. The exact current budget bounds the time-component increase by a vanishing error.
- **claim-ah-comparison-sphere** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-comparison-sphere)): There is a fixed large $C_1$ such that, at $r_1=C_1R_s$, every limit solution at $t=1$ satisfies $$\label{eq:ah-comparison-area} \mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_h(\{r=r_1\})\le C R_s^2,$$ with $C$ independent of the internal large parameters.
  - Explanation: A Green-identity comparison and the upper mass budget bound an enclosing coordinate sphere's area uniformly in the internal large parameters.
- **claim-ah-contact-selector** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-contact-selector)): For all sufficiently large $M$, at the finite parameters chosen above, there is a continuous rule $\mathfrak b$ on the uniform topology of the fields $(N,f,df,w)$ on a fixed compact original subdomain, with values in a finite convex hull in $\mathcal B_M$, such that every limit solution at $t=1$ satisfies $$\label{eq:ah-contact-majorant} \mathfrak b(N,f,df,w)>N(H_g-zk)$$ at every possible contact on $S$ of a perimeter-minimizing enclosure of $S$.
  - Explanation: Compactness and upper semicontinuity of all minimizing contact sets produce a continuous finite-convex-hull flux rule that strictly excludes boundary contact.
- **claim-ah-finite-existence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-finite-existence)): With the choices above, the system <a href="#eq:ah-system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-system">[eq:ah-system]</a>–<a href="#eq:ah-outer-data" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-outer-data">[eq:ah-outer-data]</a>, using $b_S=\mathfrak b(N,f,df,w)$, has a smooth positive solution at $t=1$ on every sufficiently large fixed truncation. Expanding truncations have a subsequence converging to a solution smooth up to $S$ on the whole exterior. It satisfies all the preceding estimates and realizes the rule $\mathfrak b$.
  - Explanation: A compact sequential elliptic map and degree continuation give finite-truncation solutions. Exhaustion yields a smooth exterior solution realizing the continuous flux rule.
- **claim-conformal-end-approximation** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-conformal-approximation)): Under <a href="#eq:stress-base-assumptions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:stress-base-assumptions">[eq:stress-base-assumptions]</a>, there are smooth metrics $g_j$ on the same exterior such that $R_{g_j}>-6$, $H_{g_j}(S)\le0$, $g_j\to g$ locally in $C^2$, and $$(1-\epsilon_j)g\le g_j\le(1+\epsilon_j)g, \quad \epsilon_j\downarrow0, \qquad p_0(g_j)\longrightarrow p_0(g). \label{eq:stress-density-convergence}$$ Each $g_j$ has the required weighted scalar integrability and finite mass fluxes. Outside a compact set, depending on $j$, it is of the form $$g_j=\phi_j^4 b,\qquad \phi_j=1+\alpha_j(\omega)r^{-3}+O(r^{-3-\xi}), \label{eq:stress-conformal-end}$$ where $\xi>0$ can be fixed and the remainder has the same decay after any fixed finite number of angular and radial-logarithmic derivatives. In particular $A_{\min}(S;g_j)\to A_{\min}(S;g)$.
  - Explanation: The original Riemannian metric admits strict-scalar approximants with a smooth conformal end, while time-component mass and minimum enclosing area converge.
- **claim-electrostatic-stress-charge** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress)): For every $M_e>0$ there is a weak solution $u$ of $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g E=0,\qquad E=e(w)\frac{\nabla u}{w},\quad w=\|du\|_g, \qquad u\|_S=-M_e,\quad u\longrightarrow0\text{ at infinity}, \label{eq:stress-electrostatics}$$ where $E=0$ at $w=0$. It satisfies $-M_e\le u\le0$, $\|u\|+\|du\|_g=O(r^{-1})$, and is $C^{1,\beta}$ locally up to $S$ and in compactified coordinates $(\rho,\omega)$ up to $\rho=0$, for some $\beta>0$, where $\rho=e^{-\eta}$. The continuous symmetric tensor $$\Pi=L(w)g-du\otimes E^\flat \label{eq:stress-tensor}$$ is distributionally divergence free, is positive definite, and obeys $$(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\Pi)^2-2\|\Pi\|_g^2=3. \label{eq:stress-algebraic-identity}$$ There is a continuous nonnegative function $e_0$ on $\mathbb S^2$ such that, uniformly in angle, $$r^2\|E\|_g\longrightarrow e_0,\qquad r^3\big(\Pi(\nu,\nu)-1\big) \longrightarrow-\tfrac12 e_0^{3/2}. \label{eq:stress-end-asymptotics}$$ Here $\nu$ points toward increasing $r$. The charge $$F_{M_e}=\int_{r=R}g(E,\nu)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_g \label{eq:stress-charge-definition}$$ is independent of large $R$, satisfies $F_{M_e}\le\int_{\mathbb S^2}e_0\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_\sigma$, and $$\liminf_{M_e\to\infty}F_{M_e}\ge A_*. \label{eq:stress-charge-saturation}$$
  - Explanation: A degenerate electrostatic potential yields a positive divergence-free stress with an exact algebraic constraint. Its asymptotic charge has a lower limit controlled by the minimum enclosing area.
- **claim-af-stress-attachment** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-af-attachment)): Let $g$ be the fixed approximating metric above. For every $\varepsilon_0>0$ there are a sufficiently large coordinate sphere $\mathcal C$, its compact connected inner region $\Omega_i$, a smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on $\Omega_i$, and a smooth scalar-flat $\mathrm{AF}$ exterior $(\Omega_o,g_o)$ attached along $\mathcal C$, with the following properties. Put $\tau_K=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g K$ and $k_T=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{\mathcal C}K$. Then $$\begin{aligned} K&<0,\qquad R_g+\tau_K^2-\|K\|_g^2 -2(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gK-d\tau_K)\cdot v>0 &&(\|v\|_g\le1), \label{eq:stress-synthetic-DEC}\\ H_i&>\|k_T\|,\qquad H_o=\sqrt{H_i^2-k_T^2}>0, \label{eq:stress-matching-curvatures}\\ m_o&\le p_0(g)-\tfrac12 a^3+\varepsilon_0. \label{eq:stress-attachment-budget} \end{aligned}$$ Here $H_i$ is the inner metric’s mean curvature on $\mathcal C$, and $H_o$ is the outer metric’s inner-boundary mean curvature, both in the direction toward the respective end. The induced metrics agree. The exterior is complete with its boundary included and has one end, with $g_o-\delta=O_k(\|x'\|^{-1})$ for every fixed $k$, where an ordinary derivative improves decay by one power. Projection from $\Omega_o$ to $\mathcal C$ along its parallel rays has upper area Jacobian at most one on every tangent two-plane.
  - Explanation: Smoothed synthetic stress and a scalar-flat parallel-surface extension produce matched boundary data and an attachment mass budget containing the cubic area contribution.
- **claim-compact-graph-construction** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-compact-solutions)): Fix base data satisfying <a href="#eq:compact-base-data" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-base-data">[eq:compact-base-data]</a>. Fix $b_*,\delta_0,\delta,a_o>0$ and $L\ge1$. For every sufficiently large finite $M$, $C_2$ can be chosen depending on these parameters, and then $\varepsilon>0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small and $D_1,D_2$ sufficiently large but finite, so that <a href="#eq:compact-system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-system">[eq:compact-system]</a>–<a href="#eq:compact-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-boundary">[eq:compact-boundary]</a> at $u_*=1$ has a positive solution on the full attached exterior. It is smooth on each closed side of $\mathcal C$ and tends to the specified values at infinity. It satisfies $$\label{eq:compact-bounds} \begin{gathered} 0\le f\le M,\qquad N_i,N_o\le C(L)M,\qquad \int_{\Omega_i}W^2\le C(L)M^2,\\ N_i\ge c\varepsilon,\qquad s_i,N_o\ge c(M,L)\varepsilon. \end{gathered}$$ The constants in these bounds do not depend on $\varepsilon,D_1,D_2$ or the outer truncation. Dependence on the fixed data and on the preceding parameters is suppressed. At fixed $M,L,\varepsilon$, the lapse and height have uniform local continuity bounds off the seam, including at $S$, independent of $D_1,D_2$. Moreover $$\label{eq:compact-penalty-targets} w\ge M^{9/10}\quad\text{where }f\ge9M/10, \qquad x\ge1\quad\text{on }\mathcal D_M\cap\{N\le2\varepsilon\},$$ and $$\label{eq:compact-penalty-cost} \int P_1\le C(L)M^{-1/10},\qquad \int P_2\le\omega_M(\varepsilon),\qquad \omega_M(\varepsilon)\longrightarrow0 \quad(\varepsilon\downarrow0).$$ The function $\omega_M$ is uniform in the finite strengths and outer radius. In particular $$\label{eq:compact-bad-volume} \int_{\mathcal D_M\cap\{x<1-\delta\}}W\le C/L,$$ where $C$ is independent of $L,M,\varepsilon,D_1,D_2$. On the smooth sides the metric $h=x\bar g$ obeys the scalar and boundary identities <a href="#eq:compact-scalar" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-scalar">[eq:compact-scalar]</a> and <a href="#eq:compact-mean-curvature" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-mean-curvature">[eq:compact-mean-curvature]</a> below. Its asymptotically flat mass satisfies $$\label{eq:compact-mass-budget} m_h\le m_o+C(b_*+\delta_0)+C(L)M^{-1/10}+C\omega_M(\varepsilon).$$ Thus the parameter order is: fix the base data; choose $b_*,\delta_0$ for the mass tolerance; choose $\delta,a_o$ and then $L$ for the area tolerance; choose $M$ large; choose $C_2$; choose $\varepsilon$ small; choose the finite strengths; and finally let the outer radius tend to infinity.
  - Explanation: The attached compact graph system has positive exterior solutions with lapse, slope, penalty, bad-volume, and mass controls after the prescribed successive choices.
- **claim-compact-lapse-slope** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-lapse)): Every such positive zero, for $0\le u_*\le1$ and sufficiently large outer radius, satisfies <a href="#eq:compact-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-bounds">[eq:compact-bounds]</a>, with $M$ replacing the upper height bound by $u_*M$. These estimates are independent of the strengths of $P_1,P_2$ and of all derivatives of $T$.
  - Explanation: A priori height, lapse, and slope controls hold along the positive continuation zeros without using penalty strengths or trace-target derivatives.
- **claim-compact-finite-penalties** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-compact-penalties)): For fixed preceding parameters the sources can be selected with finite strengths to obtain <a href="#eq:compact-penalty-targets" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-penalty-targets">[eq:compact-penalty-targets]</a>–<a href="#eq:compact-bad-volume" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-bad-volume">[eq:compact-bad-volume]</a> in every actual positive solution, uniformly in the outer truncation. Their costs obey <a href="#eq:compact-penalty-cost" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-penalty-cost">[eq:compact-penalty-cost]</a>.
  - Explanation: Finite strengths enforce the compact construction's target inequalities uniformly in outer truncation while preserving the stated integrated cost bounds.
- **claim-transmission-existence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-transmission-existence)): Fix the smooth compact base data and AF attachment of Section <a href="#sec:compact-construction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compact-construction">7</a>, with $H_i>\|k_T\|$ on $\mathcal C$, $H_g(S)\leq0$, and the smooth negative definite synthetic tensor $K$. Fix positive finite parameters and smooth cutoffs as in <a href="#eq:compact-system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-system">[eq:compact-system]</a>–<a href="#eq:compact-trace-cutoff" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-trace-cutoff">[eq:compact-trace-cutoff]</a>, including a source-free exterior collar of $\mathcal C$ and the constant $b_*>0$. Then on every sufficiently large smooth truncation there is a positive piecewise smooth solution of <a href="#eq:compact-system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-system">[eq:compact-system]</a> and <a href="#eq:compact-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-boundary">[eq:compact-boundary]</a> at $u_*=1$.* *At these fixed parameters a subsequence of such solutions as $R\to\infty$ converges smoothly on each closed side on compact subsets to a positive piecewise smooth solution on the full joined exterior. Its end values are $N_o,w\to1$. The bounds in <a href="#eq:compact-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-bounds">[eq:compact-bounds]</a> hold, and all compact-set derivative bounds are uniform in $R$. The penalty conclusions in Section <a href="#sec:compact-construction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compact-construction">7</a>, when the strengths have been chosen there, therefore hold for these solutions.
  - Explanation: Finite-parameter continuation supplies positive piecewise smooth transmission solutions on large truncations, and local compactness removes the outer boundary.
- **claim-nonlinear-seam-holder** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-seam-holder)): For the state range <a href="#eq:transmission-state-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:transmission-state-range">[eq:transmission-state-range]</a>, there are $\gamma>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that $$\\|N_i\\|_{C^\gamma(\overline\Omega_i)} +\\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\\|_{C^\gamma(\overline\Omega_i)} +\\|N_o\\|_{C^\gamma(K\cap\overline\Omega_o)}\leq C \label{eq:transmission-holder}$$ on every fixed compact set $K$. The constants are uniform over homotopy zeros and sufficiently large outer truncations. They depend on the finite state range, bounds for the undifferentiated height and lapse sources, and the fixed geometry, but not on derivatives of $T$ or the strength of $P$.
  - Explanation: Weighted energy, compatible-state flux cancellation, and excess decay yield uniform continuity of lapse and height gradient up to the nonlinear seam.
- **claim-transmission-schauder** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-transmission-schauder)): Give a height variation $\phi$ order $3$, lapse variations $u_i,u_o$ order $2$, and conformal-factor variations $v_i,v_o$ order $2$. For frozen coefficients from a state in <a href="#eq:transmission-state-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:transmission-state-range">[eq:transmission-state-range]</a>, the principal equations are $$\mathcal P:\nabla^2\phi +\frac\beta N\nabla f\cdot\nabla u_i,\qquad \Delta u_i,\quad\Delta u_o,\qquad A_i:\nabla^2v_i,\quad A_o:\nabla^2v_o. \label{eq:transmission-principal-rows}$$ Their residual norms are respectively $C^{1,\alpha}$ and $C^{0,\alpha}$ for the other four rows. The height trace has $C^{3,\alpha}$ norm. The lapse and conformal-factor value residuals have $C^{2,\alpha}$ norm, and their current-flux residuals have $C^{1,\alpha}$ norm. On a smaller fixed patch, the field norms of the indicated orders are bounded by these residual norms and the supremum norms of the fields on a larger patch. The constants are uniform on compact positive state ranges.* *At the seam the height/lapse principal conditions are <a href="#eq:transmission-frozen-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:transmission-frozen-boundary">[eq:transmission-frozen-boundary]</a>; the conformal-factor block has value continuity and positive conormal matching. At $S$ they are Dirichlet for height and Neumann for the other fields; at $S_R$ they are Dirichlet. The same estimates hold for scalar transmission with a fixed positive $C^{2,\alpha}$ value ratio, and while its outer normal-derivative coefficient is decreased to zero, the inner coefficient being kept strictly positive.
  - Explanation: Harmonic combinations establish mixed-order local transmission estimates, including the principal lapse value coupling and positive conormal matching.
- **claim-transmission-fredholm** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-transmission-fredholm)): The field derivative $D_X\mathscr F$ at each zero of <a href="#eq:transmission-nonlinear-map" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:transmission-nonlinear-map">[eq:transmission-nonlinear-map]</a> is Fredholm of index zero between <a href="#eq:transmission-domain-space" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:transmission-domain-space">[eq:transmission-domain-space]</a> and its specified residual space. Independently, the scalar density and adjoint problems with smooth base metrics, fixed $C^{1,\alpha'}$ drift, a fixed positive $C^{2,\alpha'}$ value ratio, natural flux matching, inner Neumann and outer Dirichlet data are Fredholm of index zero. Their estimates may depend on derivatives of the fixed ratio.
  - Explanation: Principal-operator deformation and finite-dimensional augmentation establish index zero, with an independent scalar density and adjoint result for fixed smooth coefficients.
- **claim-smooth-af-two-enclosures** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-af-comparison)): Let $(\Omega_i,g,K)$ and $(\Omega_o,g_o)$ be the fixed inner data and attachment of Proposition <a href="#prop:af-attachment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-attachment">30</a>, with attachment mass $m_o$. Given $0<\delta<1$ and positive tolerances $\eta_m,\eta_v,\eta_g$, the parameters of Proposition <a href="#prop:compact-solutions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:compact-solutions">31</a> can be chosen so that there is a smooth complete connected one-ended AF manifold $(X,h')$, a fixed topological cap set $O$ with $\partial O=S$, and precompact smooth open sets $E_0,E$ containing $O$ in their interiors, with the following properties.* 1. *The boundaries of $E_0$ and $E$ are compact embedded minimal surfaces. Both sets are outward minimizing, their open exteriors are connected, and $$\mathop{\mathrm{Per}}_{h'}(E_0)\le \mathop{\mathrm{Per}}_{h'}(E). \label{eq:unsafe-two-perimeters}$$ The set $E_0$ is a largest perimeter minimizing enclosure of $O$ alone, is strictly outward minimizing, and every component of $E_0$ meets $O$.* 2. *On the original side of the caps, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{h'}\ge-2,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{h'}\ge0\quad\hbox{on }X\setminus E,\qquad m_{h'}\le m_o+\eta_m . \label{eq:unsafe-comparison-output}$$ In particular the closed exterior of $E$ is smooth and complete, has exactly one AF end, and has outer minimizing minimal boundary. For any fixed $1/2<\beta<1$, its end has metric decay $O_2(\|x'\|^{-\beta})$ and scalar decay $O(\|x'\|^{-2-2\beta})$.* 3. *Identify the two original base pieces with their images in $X\setminus\operatorname{int}O$, smoothly on each closed side of the seam, and let $g_{\rm base}$ denote their respective metrics $g,g_o$. For the piecewise graph metric $h=x\bar g$, where $\bar g=g+s^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm df^2$ inside and $\bar g=g_o$ outside, one has $$(1-\eta_g)h\le h'\le(1+\eta_g)h,\qquad \bar g\ge g_{\rm base},\qquad \mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\bar g}=W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\rm base}, \label{eq:unsafe-metric-output}$$ after decreasing $\eta_g$ below one if necessary, and $$\int_{\{x<1-\delta\}}W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\rm base}<\eta_v. \label{eq:unsafe-bad-volume-output}$$ The scalar lower bound and the topology of $X\setminus \operatorname{int}O$ are independent of the large parameters.* *The order of choice is the following: choose $b_*,\delta_0$ for the mass tolerance, then $\delta$, the thin exterior omitted collar and $L$ for the volume tolerance, then $M$, then the lapse cutoff and the finite penalty strengths. The corner smoothing is chosen last, separately for each resulting fixed solution. In the enclosure construction a large fixed scaled ball radius is chosen before $M$.
  - Explanation: The smooth flat comparison has a cap-only minimizing enclosure for area transfer and an additional enclosure hiding unsafe scalar curvature for the mass theorem.
- **claim-unsafe-scale-geometry** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-unsafe-blowup)): There is a constant $C\ge1$ with the following property. For every fixed $R<\infty$, all sufficiently large $M$, and every $P\in\mathcal U_M$, the base ball of radius $Rr_P$ about $P$ does not meet the seam. In interior charts, or in charts flattened at $S$ when necessary, whose unit of base length is $r_P$, $$C^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{Id}}\le h\le C\mathop{\mathrm{Id}} \label{eq:unsafe-uniform-metric}$$ on the corresponding ball, restricted to the original side of $S$. The same comparison holds after reflection across $S$. The constant $C$ is independent of $R$; the required lower bound for $M$ may depend on $R$. Equivalently, the order of the quantifiers is $$\exists C\ \forall R<\infty\ \exists M_0(R)\ \forall M\ge M_0(R)\ \forall P\in\mathcal U_M. \label{eq:unsafe-quantifiers}$$
  - Explanation: Unsafe-point rescaling gives uniform metric comparability and excludes the seam at each fixed scaled radius. The common comparison constant precedes the radius choice.
- **claim-corner-smoothing** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-corner-smoothing)): For each sufficiently large fixed solution, the joined metric $h$ admits smooth AF replacements $h'$ on the original side of the caps such that, with errors made arbitrarily small separately at that solution, $$h'=(1+o(1))h\ \hbox{as quadratic forms},\qquad m_{h'}=m_h+o(1),\qquad H_{h'}(S)<0. \label{eq:unsafe-smoothing-estimates}$$ They satisfy $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{h'}\ge0$ off $\mathcal U_M$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}_{h'}\ge-2$ everywhere on the original side of the caps. Their AF metric and scalar decay are those of <a href="#eq:unsafe-af-decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-af-decay">[eq:unsafe-af-decay]</a>.
  - Explanation: Collar mollification and a small conformal correction smooth the corner, control the mass change, preserve the inner barrier, and retain nonnegative scalar curvature off the unsafe set.
- **claim-free-enclosures** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-free-enclosure)): Choose a sufficiently large fixed scaled radius $R_*$, then $M$ sufficiently large depending on that radius, and perform the smoothing of Lemma <a href="#lem:corner-smoothing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:corner-smoothing">40</a> sufficiently closely. There is a perimeter minimizing enclosure $E$ of $O$ and the marked balls about all points of $\mathcal U_M$, whose boundary is smooth, free, and disjoint from those balls and from $S$. There is also a largest perimeter minimizing enclosure $E_0$ of $O$ alone. These sets have all the boundary, exterior, and minimizing properties in Proposition <a href="#prop:af-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-comparison">38</a>.
  - Explanation: A fixed large scaled obstacle radius, followed by large graph height and close smoothing, forces minimizing boundaries away from unsafe balls and the original boundary.

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-elliptic-inputs",
        "exact_quote": "On fixed coordinate balls in dimension three the following estimates hold, with constants depending on the indicated ellipticity, coefficient, and geometry bounds.*\n\n1.  *Bounded measurable uniformly elliptic divergence matrices admit local subsolution bounds, weak Harnack estimates for nonnegative supersolutions, and inhomogeneous Harnack and Hölder estimates for nonnegative solutions. Bounded divergence drifts multiplying the unknown, vector forcing in $L^q$, $q>3$, and scalar forcing in $L^p$, $p>3/2$, are permitted in the corresponding estimates.*\n\n2.  *For Laplace equations with uniformly positive Lipschitz metric coefficients in interior or flattened smooth boundary charts, divergence forcing in $L^q$ gives local $W^{1,q}$ estimates. Scalar forcing in $L^2$ can be included for $3<q<6$. The same statements hold with local zero Dirichlet data or natural Neumann data, with the divergence forcing included in the conormal current. A boundary datum in $L^{p_1}$, $p_1>2$, permits a choice $3<q<3p_1/2$ sufficiently close to $3$.*\n\n3.  *Smooth-coefficient scalar Dirichlet and conormal problems have the usual Schauder estimates, including divergence-form $C^{1,\\gamma}$ estimates when the uniformly elliptic coefficients and vector forcing are $C^\\gamma$, with boundary data of the corresponding regularity. These estimates are used only after their coefficient hypotheses have been obtained.*\n\n4.  *For a bounded measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix $a$ on a ball, its positive Dirichlet Green kernel is bounded above by $C|z-z'|^{-1}$, and below by $c|z-z'|^{-1}$ when the pole and the nearby evaluation point lie in a fixed smaller ball.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.7"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-graph-curvature",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose that $\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g p=TN$, where $T$ is a smooth scalar function. Then $\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\pi=T$ and $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\bar\\nabla\\log s&=\\nabla\\log N-\\pi(v),\n \\label{eq:calculus-lapse-differential}\\\\\n R_{\\bar g}\n &=R_g+T^2-|\\pi|^2-2(\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\pi-\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dT)\\cdot v.\n \\label{eq:calculus-static-curvature}\n\\end{aligned}$$ More generally, let $\\mathcal K$ be any smooth symmetric covariant tensor, and define $$\\kappa=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\mathcal K,\\qquad\n \\ell=T-\\kappa,\\qquad \\lambda=\\pi-\\mathcal K,\n \\qquad C=\\lambda-\\ell g,\n \\label{eq:calculus-trace-definitions}$$ and $$\\mathscr D(v)=R_g+\\kappa^2-|\\mathcal K|^2\n       -2(\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\mathcal K-\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\kappa)\\cdot v.\n \\label{eq:calculus-dominant-expression}$$ Then $$R_{\\bar g}=\\mathscr D(v)+|\\lambda|^2-\\ell^2\n                   -\\frac2N\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp).\n \\label{eq:calculus-completed-curvature}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.7"
      },

\\label{eq:calculus-general-system}$$ Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n Q&=N\\bar\\nabla x+xCp-(x-1)B,\\notag\\\\\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g Q&=\\Phi-\\Psi,\n \\label{eq:calculus-general-current}\\\\\n +6(x-1)^2+\\frac{2P}{N}.\n \\label{eq:calculus-ah-curvature}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For the constraint densities in <a href=\"#eq:constraints\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\"         "anchor": "stmt-lem-graph-boundary",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal S$ be a smooth two-sided hypersurface on which $f$ is constant. Choose a $g$-unit normal $n$, and write $H=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_{\\mathcal S}n$, $\\hat z=v\\cdot n$, $y=\\hat z^2$, and $k_T=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{\\mathcal S}\\mathcal K$. The same directed normal is used on each side if $\\mathcal S$ is a gluing face. Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n d^2\\partial_n\\log s&=B_n/N-k_T\\hat z+yH,\n \\label{eq:calculus-boundary-lapse}\\\\\n s\\sqrt{x}\\,H_h\n &=N(H-k_T\\hat z)+B_n+(A\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dw)_n/x.\n \\label{eq:calculus-boundary}\n\\end{aligned}$$ In particular, in the maximal AH system with $v=-z n$, $k=K(n,n)$, $B_n=-b_S$, and $(A\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dw)_n=0$, $$s\\sqrt{x}\\,H_h=N(H-zk)-b_S=NH+\\partial_nN.\n \\label{eq:calculus-ah-boundary}$$ In the compact system, if $H\\le0$, $k_T<0$, $\\hat z\\le0$, $B_n=-b_*<0$, and $(A\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dw)_n=0$, then $H_h<0$.*\n\n*Suppose, at a compact gluing face, that $N_o=s_i$, that $w$ and the normal fluxes of $B,A\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dw$ agree, that $f$ is constant on the inner face, and that $p=0$ outside. The induced $h$-metrics then agree. If the inner base mean curvature satisfies $H_i>|k_T|$ and the outer one is $H_o=\\sqrt{H_i^2-k_T^2}$, then $H_{h,i}\\ge H_{h,o}$, both measured toward the end.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-gradient-maximum",
        "exact_quote": "Let $N>0,f,\\mathcal K,T$ be smooth and satisfy $\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g p=TN$ and $\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g[\\nabla N-(\\mathcal K+\\ell g)p]=\\Phi$, with the definitions above. Suppose on the region in question that $$|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g|+|\\mathcal K|+\n       |\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\mathcal K-\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\mathcal K|+|T|\\le C_0,\n \\qquad \\Phi\\le C_0N+\\Sigma,\\qquad \\Sigma\\ge0.\n \\label{eq:calculus-maximum-hypotheses}$$ At a point where $m=|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm df|>0$, set $$\\begin{aligned}\n l&=\\log m,\\quad u=\\log N,\\quad e=\\nabla f/m,\\quad y=|v|^2,\\\\\n q&=\\frac{1-y}{1+y},\\quad \\beta=1+q,\\quad\n \\mathcal P=g^{-1}+(q-1)e\\otimes e,\\quad G=-\\log s.\n \\end{aligned}\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-notation}$$ Let $j$ be twice continuously differentiable with $j''>0$, with either sign allowed for $j'$, and let $\\eta$ be a twice continuously differentiable localization function. At an interior local maximum of $G+j(f)+\\eta$ with $y\\ge1/2$, $$j''q m^2\\le C\\left[1+\\frac\\Sigma N\n       +(1-y)^2(j'm)^2+|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\eta|^2+|\\nabla^2\\eta|\\right],\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-maximum}$$ where $C$ depends only on $C_0$. In particular, at that point, $$W^2\\le\\frac C{j''}\\left[\n     N^2+N\\Sigma+(j')^2\n       +N^2\\bigl(|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\eta|^2+|\\nabla^2\\eta|\\bigr)\\right].\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-weighted}$$ No positive lower bound for $N$, no derivative bound for $T$, and no second derivative bound for $N$ enter these two estimates.*\n\n\n\n*At a constant-height boundary, with the notation of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:graph-boundary\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:graph-boundary\">11</a>, the exact normal derivative is $$d^2\\partial_n\\bigl(G+j(f)+\\eta\\bigr)\n   =-B_n/N+k_T\\hat z-yH+j'\\hat z/N+d^2\\partial_n\\eta.\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-boundary}$$ For the maximal AH inner boundary, if $H\\le k$, $b_S\\ge0$, and $v=-zn$, this implies $$G_n=-\\frac{yH+u_n}{1-y}\n       =\\frac{b_S/N+zk-z^2H}{1-z^2}\n       \\ge\\frac{zk}{1+z}.\n \\label{eq:calculus-ah-gradient-boundary}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.7"
      },

Suppose on the region in question that $$|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g|+|\\mathcal K|+\n       |\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\mathcal K-\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\mathcal K|+|T|\\le C_0,\n \\qquad \\Phi\\le C_0N+\\Sigma,\\qquad \\Sigma\\ge0.\n \\label{eq:calculus-maximum-hypotheses}$$ At a point where $m=|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm df|>0$, set $$\\begin{aligned}\n l&=\\log m,\\quad u=\\log N,\\quad e=\\nabla f/m,\\quad y=|v|^2,\\\\\n q&=\\frac{1-y}{1+y},\\quad \\beta=1+q,\\quad\n \\mathcal P=g^{-1}+(q-1)e\\otimes e,\\quad G=-\\log s.\n \\end{aligned}\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-notation}$$ Let $j$ be twice continuously differentiable with $j''>0$, with either sign allowed for $j'$, and let $\\eta$ be a twice continuously differentiable localization function. At an interior local maximum of $G+j(f)+\\eta$ with $y\\ge1/2$, $$j''q m^2\\le C\\left[1+\\frac\\Sigma N\n       +(1-y)^2(j'm)^2+|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\eta|^2+|\\nabla^2\\eta|\\right],\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-maximum}$$ where $C$ depends only on $C_0$. In particular, at that point, $$W^2\\le\\frac C{j''}\\left[\n     N^2+N\\Sigma+(j')^2\n       +N^2\\bigl(|\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm d\\eta|^2+|\\nabla^2\\eta|\\bigr)\\right].\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-weighted}$$ No positive lower bound for $N$, no derivative bound for $T$, and no second derivative bound for $N$ enter these two estimates.*\n\n\n\n*At a constant-height boundary, with the notation of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:graph-boundary\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:graph-boundary\">11</a>, the exact normal derivative is $$d^2\\partial_n\\bigl(G+j(f)+\\eta\\bigr)\n   =-B_n/N+k_T\\hat z-yH+j'\\hat z/N+d^2\\partial_n\\eta.\n \\label{eq:calculus-gradient-boundary}$$ For the maximal AH inner boundary, if $H\\le k$, $b_S\\ge0$, and $v=-zn$, this implies $$G_n=-\\frac{yH+u_n}{1-y}\n       =\\frac{b_S/N+zk-z^2H}{1-z^2}\n       \\ge\\frac{zk}{1+z}.\n \\label{eq:calculus-ah-gradient-boundary}$$",

        "exact_quote": "In the setting of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:gradient-energy\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:gradient-energy\">13</a>, let $\\mathcal T_f=\\nabla^2f-(\\Delta f)g$. The exact smooth vector identity is $$\\rho\\mathcal P\\nabla G\n   =-\\frac{\\nabla N}{s}\n      +\\mathcal T_f\\left(\\frac{s^3}{N}\\nabla f\\right)\n      +Ts\\nabla f,\n \\qquad\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\mathcal T_f=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g(\\nabla f,\\cdot).\n \\label{eq:calculus-newton}$$ The coefficient of $\\mathcal T_f$ is smooth at $\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm df=0$.*\n\n\n\n\n*More specifically, in a fixed smooth face chart take compatible reference fields $\\mathcal V_*=(n_*,a_*\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dt,s_*)$ for $\\mathcal V=(N_i,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm df,N_o)$, where $t$ is inner signed unit normal distance, $n_*>0$, and $s_*=s(n_*,|a_*|)$. Assume the reference ranges and the actual fields lie in a fixed bounded positive lapse and finite slope range. Put $Y_*=s_*^{-k_0}$ and $$c_*=(k_0Y_*/s_*) ,\\qquad\n \\mathfrak b_*=k_0Y_*\\frac{s_*^3}{n_*}a_*\\nabla t.$$ For the following assertion assume also that $\\Phi$ is bounded on each side. Modify the inner and outer energy fluxes by $$\\mathcal J_i=\\rho\\mathcal P\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dY+c_*B-\\mathcal T_f\\mathfrak b_* ,\n \\qquad \\mathcal J_o=\\nabla Y+c_*B.\n \\label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux}$$ They have bounded directed flux difference across the face, and $$\\begin{aligned}\n |\\mathcal J|&\\le C\\bigl(1+|\\mathcal V-\\mathcal V_*|\\sqrt E\\bigr),\n \\label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux-size}\\\\\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}\\mathcal J&\\ge c'E-C-C\\delta_{\\mathcal C}\n \\label{eq:calculus-frozen-flux-divergence}\n\\end{aligned}$$ in the joined weak formulation, with $E=E_i$ inside and $E=|\\nabla N_o|^2$ outside. The second line is understood with the smooth metric densities in coordinates, and $\\delta_{\\mathcal C}$ is surface measure on the face.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-area-transfer",
        "exact_quote": "Fix the capped topology $(X,O)$, a number $A_*>0$, and a scalar lower bound $C_R\\ge0$. Suppose a comparison has the following properties.*\n\n1.  *The smooth complete metric $\\widehat h$ has one $\\ensuremath{\\mathrm{AH}}$ or $\\ensuremath{\\mathrm{AF}}$ end with the mean-curvature and radial-gradient asymptotics used in <a href=\"#eq:flow-end-subsolution\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:flow-end-subsolution\">[eq:flow-end-subsolution]</a>. The cap-only enclosure $E_0$ is a smooth precompact strictly outward-minimizing set, with minimal boundary disjoint from $O$, every component meeting $O$, and $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Scal}}_{\\widehat h}\\ge-C_R$ outside $E_0$.*\n\n\n2.  *On $X\\setminus O$ there are a reference metric $g_{\\mathrm{base}}$, positive functions $x,W$, a metric $\\bar g$, and a weight $0<\\rho\\le1$, such that $$\\label{eq:flow-metric-comparison}\n     \\bar g\\ge g_{\\mathrm{base}},\\qquad\n     \\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dV_{\\bar g}=W\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dV_{g_{\\mathrm{base}}},\\qquad\n     (1-\\eta)x\\bar g\\le\\widehat h\\le(1+\\eta)x\\bar g.$$*\n\n\n3.  *Every enclosing $C^1$ surface with connected exterior, as in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:area-projection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:area-projection\">18</a>, satisfies $$\\label{eq:flow-abstract-projection}\n     \\int_N\\rho\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dA_{g_{\\mathrm{base}}}\\ge(1-q)A_*.$$ In the piecewise case this is required for surfaces having zero area in the joining surface.*\n\n\n*For every $0<\\varepsilon<1$ there are positive tolerances $\\eta_0,q_0,\\delta_0$ and $v_0$, depending only on $\\varepsilon,A_*,C_R$ and the integer $b_2$ in <a href=\"#eq:flow-topology-constant\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:flow-topology-constant\">[eq:flow-topology-constant]</a>, with the following consequence. If $\\eta\\le\\eta_0$, $q\\le q_0$, $0<\\delta\\le\\delta_0$, and $$\\label{eq:flow-bad-volume}\n \\int_{\\{x<1-\\delta\\}}\\rho^{3/2}W\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dV_{g_{\\mathrm{base}}}<v_0,$$ then $$\\label{eq:flow-area-conclusion}\n |\\partial E_0|_{\\widehat h}\\ge(1-\\varepsilon)A_*.$$ The tolerances are uniform over all comparisons satisfying these conditions; the geometry and initial area of $E_0$ may vary.",

      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-ah-reduction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $F:[0,\\infty)\\to[0,\\infty)$ be continuous and nondecreasing. Suppose that every smooth, complete, connected, orientable, one-ended asymptotically hyperbolic three-dimensional exterior with nonempty compact minimal boundary, scalar curvature at least $-6$, $g-b\\in C^{2,\\gamma}_\\tau$ for some $0<\\gamma<1$ and $3/2<\\tau<3$, the weighted scalar integrability of Section <a href=\"#sec:hypotheses\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:hypotheses\">1</a>, and four finite mass fluxes satisfies $$p_0\\ge F(A_{\\min}).$$ The exponent $\\gamma$ may depend on the comparison metric. This hypothesis is to hold in every designated asymptotic chart, without a causal-character assumption on the mass covector. Then every maximal initial-data exterior of Section <a href=\"#sec:hypotheses\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:hypotheses\">1</a> satisfies, in each designated chart, $$p_0(g)\\ge F\\bigl(A_{\\min}(S;g)\\bigr).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.7"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-ah-lapse",
        "exact_quote": "For smooth solutions on sufficiently large truncations, uniformly over $0\\le t\\le1$ and $b_S\\in\\mathcal B_M$, $$\\label{eq:ah-lapse-bounds}\n N\\le Cr,\\qquad N\\ge c(M)\\epsilon r,\\qquad\n \\frac{|N-V_0|}{r}\\le\n C(R_s/r)^{1+\\kappa}\\quad(r\\ge2R_s),$$ where $0<\\kappa<\\tau-1$ is fixed and small. The upper constant uses only the $L^{p_1}$ bound of $b_S$. On compact sets, $N$ has uniform Hölder and $W^{1,q}$ bounds for some $q>3$, depending on $M,L$, but independent of $\\epsilon,d_*$ and derivatives of $b_S$.*\n\n*The positivity and lower bound remain true at a fixed point in which the drift $Z=K(v)$ is computed using a smooth positive extension of the constitutive lapse argument, provided that the actual lapse equation is $\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g(\\nabla N-ZN)=3N+\\Sigma$ and the cutoff $N\\le\\epsilon$ uses the actual lapse.",

      "exact_statement": "Under <a href=\"#eq:stress-base-assumptions\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:stress-base-assumptions\">[eq:stress-base-assumptions]</a>, there are smooth metrics $g_j$ on the same exterior such that $R_{g_j}>-6$, $H_{g_j}(S)\\le0$, $g_j\\to g$ locally in $C^2$, and $$(1-\\epsilon_j)g\\le g_j\\le(1+\\epsilon_j)g,\n \\quad \\epsilon_j\\downarrow0,\n \\qquad p_0(g_j)\\longrightarrow p_0(g).\n \\label{eq:stress-density-convergence}$$ Each $g_j$ has the required weighted scalar integrability and finite mass fluxes.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress",
        "exact_quote": "For every $M_e>0$ there is a weak solution $u$ of $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g E=0,\\qquad\n E=e(w)\\frac{\\nabla u}{w},\\quad w=|du|_g,\n \\qquad u|_S=-M_e,\\quad u\\longrightarrow0\\text{ at infinity},\n \\label{eq:stress-electrostatics}$$ where $E=0$ at $w=0$. It satisfies $-M_e\\le u\\le0$, $|u|+|du|_g=O(r^{-1})$, and is $C^{1,\\beta}$ locally up to $S$ and in compactified coordinates $(\\rho,\\omega)$ up to $\\rho=0$, for some $\\beta>0$, where $\\rho=e^{-\\eta}$. The continuous symmetric tensor $$\\Pi=L(w)g-du\\otimes E^\\flat\n \\label{eq:stress-tensor}$$ is distributionally divergence free, is positive definite, and obeys $$(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\Pi)^2-2|\\Pi|_g^2=3.\n \\label{eq:stress-algebraic-identity}$$ There is a continuous nonnegative function $e_0$ on $\\mathbb S^2$ such that, uniformly in angle, $$r^2|E|_g\\longrightarrow e_0,\\qquad\n r^3\\big(\\Pi(\\nu,\\nu)-1\\big)\n       \\longrightarrow-\\tfrac12 e_0^{3/2}.\n \\label{eq:stress-end-asymptotics}$$ Here $\\nu$ points toward increasing $r$. The charge $$F_{M_e}=\\int_{r=R}g(E,\\nu)\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dA_g\n \\label{eq:stress-charge-definition}$$ is independent of large $R$, satisfies $F_{M_e}\\le\\int_{\\mathbb S^2}e_0\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dA_\\sigma$, and $$\\liminf_{M_e\\to\\infty}F_{M_e}\\ge A_*.\n \\label{eq:stress-charge-saturation}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.7"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-af-attachment",
        "exact_quote": "Let $g$ be the fixed approximating metric above. For every $\\varepsilon_0>0$ there are a sufficiently large coordinate sphere $\\mathcal C$, its compact connected inner region $\\Omega_i$, a smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on $\\Omega_i$, and a smooth scalar-flat $\\mathrm{AF}$ exterior $(\\Omega_o,g_o)$ attached along $\\mathcal C$, with the following properties. Put $\\tau_K=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g K$ and $k_T=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{\\mathcal C}K$. Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n K&<0,\\qquad\n R_g+\\tau_K^2-|K|_g^2\n   -2(\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_gK-d\\tau_K)\\cdot v>0\n       &&(|v|_g\\le1),\n \\label{eq:stress-synthetic-DEC}\\\\\n H_i&>|k_T|,\\qquad\n H_o=\\sqrt{H_i^2-k_T^2}>0,\n \\label{eq:stress-matching-curvatures}\\\\\n m_o&\\le p_0(g)-\\tfrac12 a^3+\\varepsilon_0.\n \\label{eq:stress-attachment-budget}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $H_i$ is the inner metric’s mean curvature on $\\mathcal C$, and $H_o$ is the outer metric’s inner-boundary mean curvature, both in the direction toward the respective end. The induced metrics agree. The exterior is complete with its boundary included and has one end, with $g_o-\\delta=O_k(|x'|^{-1})$ for every fixed $k$, where an ordinary derivative improves decay by one power. Projection from $\\Omega_o$ to $\\mathcal C$ along its parallel rays has upper area Jacobian at most one on every tangent two-plane.",

        "exact_quote": "Fix base data satisfying <a href=\"#eq:compact-base-data\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-base-data\">[eq:compact-base-data]</a>. Fix $b_*,\\delta_0,\\delta,a_o>0$ and $L\\ge1$. For every sufficiently large finite $M$, $C_2$ can be chosen depending on these parameters, and then $\\varepsilon>0$ can be chosen arbitrarily small and $D_1,D_2$ sufficiently large but finite, so that <a href=\"#eq:compact-system\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-system\">[eq:compact-system]</a>–<a href=\"#eq:compact-boundary\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-boundary\">[eq:compact-boundary]</a> at $u_*=1$ has a positive solution on the full attached exterior. It is smooth on each closed side of $\\mathcal C$ and tends to the specified values at infinity. It satisfies $$\\label{eq:compact-bounds}\n \\begin{gathered}\n 0\\le f\\le M,\\qquad N_i,N_o\\le C(L)M,\\qquad\n \\int_{\\Omega_i}W^2\\le C(L)M^2,\\\\\n N_i\\ge c\\varepsilon,\\qquad s_i,N_o\\ge c(M,L)\\varepsilon.\n \\end{gathered}$$ The constants in these bounds do not depend on $\\varepsilon,D_1,D_2$ or the outer truncation. Dependence on the fixed data and on the preceding parameters is suppressed. At fixed $M,L,\\varepsilon$, the lapse and height have uniform local continuity bounds off the seam, including at $S$, independent of $D_1,D_2$. Moreover $$\\label{eq:compact-penalty-targets}\n w\\ge M^{9/10}\\quad\\text{where }f\\ge9M/10,\n \\qquad x\\ge1\\quad\\text{on }\\mathcal D_M\\cap\\{N\\le2\\varepsilon\\},$$ and $$\\label{eq:compact-penalty-cost}\n \\int P_1\\le C(L)M^{-1/10},\\qquad\n \\int P_2\\le\\omega_M(\\varepsilon),\\qquad \\omega_M(\\varepsilon)\\longrightarrow0\n \\quad(\\varepsilon\\downarrow0).$$ The function $\\omega_M$ is uniform in the finite strengths and outer radius. In particular $$\\label{eq:compact-bad-volume}\n \\int_{\\mathcal D_M\\cap\\{x<1-\\delta\\}}W\\le C/L,$$ where $C$ is independent of $L,M,\\varepsilon,D_1,D_2$. On the smooth sides the metric $h=x\\bar g$ obeys the scalar and boundary identities <a href=\"#eq:compact-scalar\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-scalar\">[eq:compact-scalar]</a> and <a href=\"#eq:compact-mean-curvature\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-mean-curvature\">[eq:compact-mean-curvature]</a> below. Its asymptotically flat mass satisfies $$\\label{eq:compact-mass-budget}\n m_h\\le m_o+C(b_*+\\delta_0)+C(L)M^{-1/10}+C\\omega_M(\\varepsilon).$$ Thus the parameter order is: fix the base data; choose $b_*,\\delta_0$ for the mass tolerance; choose $\\delta,a_o$ and then $L$ for the area tolerance; choose $M$ large; choose $C_2$; choose $\\varepsilon$ small; choose the finite strengths; and finally let the outer radius tend to infinity.",

        "exact_quote": "Give a height variation $\\phi$ order $3$, lapse variations $u_i,u_o$ order $2$, and conformal-factor variations $v_i,v_o$ order $2$. The height trace has $C^{3,\\alpha}$ norm. The lapse and conformal-factor value residuals have $C^{2,\\alpha}$ norm, and their current-flux residuals have $C^{1,\\alpha}$ norm. On a smaller fixed patch, the field norms of the indicated orders are bounded by these residual norms and the supremum norms of the fields on a larger patch. At $S$ they are Dirichlet for height and Neumann for the other fields; at $S_R$ they are Dirichlet.
