<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Hyperbolic background and static potentials** ([source](#eq:background)): Write $$\label{eq:background} b=\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm dr^2}{1+r^2}+r^2\sigma, \qquad \eta=\operatorname{arsinh}r, \qquad V_0=\sqrt{1+r^2},\qquad V_i=r\omega_i\quad(1\le i\le3),$$ where $\sigma$ is the unit round metric and $\omega_i$ are the coordinate functions of the unit sphere.
- **Weighted tensor Hölder spaces** ([source](#pm-h-3)): On the end, a tensor belongs to $C^{k,\alpha}_\tau$ if its $b$-covariant derivatives through order $k$ are $O(e^{-\tau\eta})$, and its order-$k$ local Hölder seminorms on uniform $b$-unit coordinate balls have the same weight.
- **Mass flux covector** ([source](#eq:ah-mass)): For $e=g-b$, define the mass fluxes in the chosen chart by $$\begin{aligned} \label{eq:ah-mass} p_\mu(g)&=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\{r=R\}}\mathbb U(V_\mu,e)(\nu_b)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_b, &&0\le\mu\le3,\\ \mathbb U(V,e)&=V(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_b e-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_b e) +(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_b e)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV-e(\nabla_b V,\cdot). \label{eq:mass-integrand} \end{aligned}$$
- **Invariant hyperbolic mass** ([source](#eq:invariant-mass)): When the covector is future timelike, its invariant mass is $$\label{eq:invariant-mass} m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g)=\sqrt{p_0(g)^2-p_1(g)^2-p_2(g)^2-p_3(g)^2}, \qquad p_0(g)>\sqrt{p_1(g)^2+p_2(g)^2+p_3(g)^2}.$$
- **Maximal constraints and matter densities** ([source](#eq:constraints)): Maximality and the noncosmological constraint densities are $$\label{eq:constraints} \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0, \qquad 16\pi\mu=R_g+6-\|K\|_g^2, \qquad 8\pi J_i=\nabla_g^jK_{ij}.$$
- **Future outer null expansion** ([source](#eq:future-trapping)): Set $$\label{eq:future-trapping} H=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=(g^{ij}-\nu^i\nu^j)K_{ij}, \qquad \theta_+=H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK.$$
- **Admissible end-side domains and minimum enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-def-minimum-area)): An admissible end-side domain is a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega$, closed as a subset of $\Omega$, such that $$\operatorname{int}D\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega \quad\hbox{and}\quad \{r>R\}\subset D\quad\hbox{for some }R.$$ Its entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\partial D$ must be compact, smooth, embedded, and two-sided, with any portions coinciding with $S$ included. Define $$\label{eq:minimum-area} A_{\min}(S;g)=\inf_D\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\partial D).$$ In particular $D=\Omega$ is admissible and contributes $\partial D=S$. An empty relative frontier is not an admissible replacement for this intrinsic boundary.
- **ADM mass normalization** ([source](#eq:adm-mass)): For an AF metric $h$ in a Euclidean end chart $y$, our normalization is $$\label{eq:adm-mass} m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h)=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|y\|=R}(\partial_jh_{ij}-\partial_ih_{jj}) n^i\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{\mathrm{Eucl}}.$$
- **Static graph constitutive fields** ([source](#sec:graph-calculus)): For a positive smooth function $N$ and a smooth function $f$, define $s>0$ and $p$ by $$p=s^2\nabla f,\qquad s^2+\|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\|^2s^4=N^2, \qquad v=\frac pN,\qquad W=\frac Ns, \qquad \bar g=g+s^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\otimes\mathop{}\!\mathrm df. \label{eq:calculus-constitutive}$$
- **Conformal graph metric and graph second form** ([source](#sec:graph-calculus)): For a further positive function $w$ put $$x=sw,\qquad h=x\bar g,\qquad A=Ns\bar g^{-1}, \qquad \pi=N^{-1}\operatorname{sym}\nabla p^\flat, \label{eq:calculus-conformal-definitions}$$ where $\operatorname{sym}$ is the half-sum.
- **Fixed exterior topology constant** ([source](#eq:flow-topology-constant)): In particular, $$\label{eq:flow-topology-constant} b_2=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(X\setminus\operatorname{int}O;\mathbb F_2)<\infty.$$
- **Weak-flow levels and area** ([source](#pm-h-18)): For positive-time notation, extend the exterior level function $u$ by zero on the initial set and, for $t>0$, write $$\label{eq:flow-levels} E_t=E_0\cup\{u<t\},\qquad N_t=\partial E_t,\qquad A(t)=\|N_t\|_{\widetilde h}=e^t A(0).$$
- **Electrostatic Legendre law** ([source](#pm-h-34)): For $0\le e\le1$ define $$t(e)=\sqrt{1-e^{3/2}},\qquad L(w)=\max_{0\le e\le1}\{t(e)+we\},\qquad w\ge0. \label{eq:stress-legendre-law}$$
- **Electrostatic stress tensor** ([source](#pm-h-34)): The continuous symmetric tensor $$\Pi=L(w)g-du\otimes E^\flat \label{eq:stress-tensor}$$ is distributionally divergence free, is positive definite, and obeys $$(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\Pi)^2-2\|\Pi\|_g^2=3. \label{eq:stress-algebraic-identity}$$
- **Electrostatic charge** ([source](#eq:stress-charge-definition)): The charge $$F_{M_e}=\int_{r=R}g(E,\nu)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_g \label{eq:stress-charge-definition}$$ is independent of large $R$, satisfies $F_{M_e}\le\int_{\mathbb S^2}e_0\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_\sigma$, and $$\liminf_{M_e\to\infty}F_{M_e}\ge A_*. \label{eq:stress-charge-saturation}$$
- **Unsafe scalar-curvature set** ([source](#eq:unsafe-scalar-support)): Define $\mathcal U_M\subset\overline\Omega_i$ by the closed versions of the four trace-cutoff inequalities in <a href="#eq:compact-trace-cutoff" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-trace-cutoff">[eq:compact-trace-cutoff]</a>, together with $N_i\ge\delta_0$.
- **Unsafe-point scale** ([source](#pm-h-43)): At $P\in\mathcal U_M$, set $$N_0=N_i(P),\qquad r_P=x(P)^{-1/2}. \label{eq:unsafe-scale}$$

| q-flow-euler-characteristic | \chi(N_t) | ≤ | $2b_2$ | Fixed second homology of the capped exterior. |

| q-ah-boundary-penalty-scale | T | = | $M^{4/5}$ | Finite target selected before the lapse cutoff and penalty strengths. |
| q-ah-volume-penalty-scale | L | = | $M^2$ | Large finite graph height. |

| q-ah-first-penalty-cost | \int_{\Omega_R}P_1\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g | ≤ | $C T/M$ | Uniform in outer truncation, allowable boundary datum, and strengths. |
| q-electrostatic-stress-identity | (\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\Pi)^2-2\|\Pi\|_g^2 | = | $3$ | Pointwise algebraic identity at finite gradient. |
| q-electrostatic-charge-saturation | \liminf_{M_e\to\infty}F_{M_e} | ≥ | $A_*$ | Potential height tends to infinity after fixing the original metric. |
| q-attachment-mass-budget | m_o | ≤ | $p_0(g)-\tfrac12 a^3+\varepsilon_0$ | Choose electrostatic height, then attachment sphere, then compact stress smoothing. |
| q-compact-height-energy | \int_{\Omega_i}W^2 | ≤ | $C(L)M^2$ | Independent of subsequent lapse cutoff, penalty strengths, and outer truncation. |
| q-compact-designated-bad-volume | \int_{\mathcal D_M\cap\{x<1-\delta\}}W | ≤ | $C/L$ | The stated constant is independent of the volume penalty and all subsequent large or small parameters. |
| q-compact-mass-budget | m_h | ≤ | $m_o+C(b_*+\delta_0)+C(L)M^{-1/10}+C\omega_M(\varepsilon)$ | Successive finite parameter choices in the prescribed order. |

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress",
          "exact_quote": "For every $M_e>0$ there is a weak solution $u$ of $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g E=0,\\qquad\n E=e(w)\\frac{\\nabla u}{w},\\quad w=|du|_g,\n \\qquad u|_S=-M_e,\\quad u\\longrightarrow0\\text{ at infinity},\n \\label{eq:stress-electrostatics}$$ where $E=0$ at $w=0$.         {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-af-attachment",
          "exact_quote": "Let $g$ be the fixed approximating metric above. For every $\\varepsilon_0>0$ there are a sufficiently large coordinate sphere $\\mathcal C$, its compact connected inner region $\\Omega_i$, a smooth symmetric tensor $K$ on $\\Omega_i$, and a smooth scalar-flat $\\mathrm{AF}$ exterior $(\\Omega_o,g_o)$ attached along $\\mathcal C$, with the following properties. Put $\\tau_K=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g K$ and $k_T=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{\\mathcal C}K$. Then $$\\begin{aligned}\n K&<0,\\qquad\n R_g+\\tau_K^2-|K|_g^2\n   -2(\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_gK-d\\tau_K)\\cdot v>0\n       &&(|v|_g\\le1),\n \\label{eq:stress-synthetic-DEC}\\\\\n H_i&>|k_T|,\\qquad\n H_o=\\sqrt{H_i^2-k_T^2}>0,\n \\label{eq:stress-matching-curvatures}\\\\\n m_o&\\le p_0(g)-\\tfrac12 a^3+\\varepsilon_0.\n \\label{eq:stress-attachment-budget}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $H_i$ is the inner metric’s mean curvature on $\\mathcal C$, and $H_o$ is the outer metric’s inner-boundary mean curvature, both in the direction toward the respective end. The induced metrics agree. The exterior is complete with its boundary included and has one end, with $g_o-\\delta=O_k(|x'|^{-1})$ for every fixed $k$, where an ordinary derivative improves decay by one power. Projection from $\\Omega_o$ to $\\mathcal C$ along its parallel rays has upper area Jacobian at most one on every tangent two-plane.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.7"
        }

In particular $$\\label{eq:compact-bad-volume}\n \\int_{\\mathcal D_M\\cap\\{x<1-\\delta\\}}W\\le C/L,$$ where $C$ is independent of $L,M,\\varepsilon,D_1,D_2$. On the smooth sides the metric $h=x\\bar g$ obeys the scalar and boundary identities <a href=\"#eq:compact-scalar\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-scalar\">[eq:compact-scalar]</a> and <a href=\"#eq:compact-mean-curvature\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:compact-mean-curvature\">[eq:compact-mean-curvature]</a> below. Its asymptotically flat mass satisfies $$\\label{eq:compact-mass-budget}\n m_h\\le m_o+C(b_*+\\delta_0)+C(L)M^{-1/10}+C\\omega_M(\\varepsilon).$$ Thus the parameter order is: fix the base data; choose $b_*,\\delta_0$ for the mass tolerance; choose $\\delta,a_o$ and then $L$ for the area tolerance; choose $M$ large; choose $C_2$; choose $\\varepsilon$ small; choose the finite strengths; and finally let the outer radius tend to infinity.",

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-compact-core** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-core) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-core): End separation, completeness, and orientable handlebody gluing. -> Connected compact truncations and a capped ambient manifold.
- **step-cut-enclosures** [claim](#stmt-lem-cut-enclosure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cut-enclosure): Complementation, local boundary coordinates, and perimeter lower semicontinuity. -> Cut-to-enclosure correspondence and the outward-minimizing area identification.
- **step-mass-covariance** [claim](#stmt-prop-mass-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-mass-covariance): Static scalar linearization, integrable flux divergence, and Lorentz normal form. -> Covariant mass fluxes and an admissible original rest chart.
- **step-af-penrose-input** [claim](#stmt-thm-af-penrose) / [proof](#pm-h-9): Invoke the published asymptotically flat Riemannian Penrose inequality in the stated normalization. -> Mass lower bound in terms of total boundary area.
- **step-scalar-local-inputs** [claim](#stmt-prop-elliptic-inputs) / [proof](#pm-h-10): Use the separately stated local scalar elliptic estimates under their coefficient hypotheses. -> Local bounds, continuity, Laplace estimates, Schauder estimates, and Green comparison.
- **step-graph-curvature** [claim](#stmt-lem-graph-curvature) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-graph-curvature): Differentiate the constitutive relation, apply contracted Gauss–Codazzi identities, and complete the square. -> Static and completed graph scalar-curvature identities.
- **step-graph-current** [claim](#stmt-lem-graph-current) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-graph-current): Cancel height-scale derivatives in the current and substitute the conformal scalar-curvature formula. -> Exact current and scalar identities for both deformation systems.
- **step-graph-boundary** [claim](#stmt-lem-graph-boundary) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-graph-boundary): Use constant height to reduce tangential Hessians and compare directed normal curvatures. -> Boundary curvature formulas and seam mean-curvature ordering.
- **step-gradient-maximum** [claim](#stmt-lem-gradient-maximum) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-gradient-maximum): Differentiate the height equation, cancel trace-target derivatives with the lapse equation, and use a localized maximum. -> Tilt bounds without lapse floors or trace-target derivative bounds.
- **step-gradient-energy** [claim](#stmt-lem-gradient-energy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-gradient-energy): Extract the positive quadratic form and exponentiate the negative logarithmic scale. -> Coercive differential energy inequalities and bounded seam flux discrepancy.
- **step-newton-current** [claim](#stmt-lem-newton-flux) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-newton-flux): Use the Newton tensor divergence identity and freeze coefficients at compatible states. -> A modified current small near a reference state and coercive in divergence.
- **step-flow-initial-adjustment** [claim](#stmt-lem-flow-initial-adjustment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-flow-initial-adjustment): Apply a compactly supported conformal collar factor increasing only on the exterior. -> Positive initial mean curvature with unchanged area and controlled scalar lower bound.
- **step-flow-topology** [claim](#stmt-lem-hull-components) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hull-components): Exclude new components variationally, fill bounded complement components, and use homological intersection pairings. -> Connected exterior and topology-controlled level-boundary component counts.
- **step-flow-curvature** [claim](#stmt-lem-flow-curvature) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-flow-curvature): Combine weak-flow growth, Gauss–Bonnet, the scalar lower bound, and an integrating factor. -> Uniform curvature-energy bound independent of initial area.
- **step-area-projection** [claim](#stmt-lem-area-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-area-projection): Project discarded end portions to a cutting sphere or along convex parallel rays and round corners. -> Weighted original enclosing-area lower bounds for comparison surfaces.
- **step-uniform-area-transfer** [claim](#stmt-prop-area-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-area-transfer): Assume an area deficit, follow a fixed relative-area window, and combine Hölder with weighted coarea. -> Uniform preservation of the cap-only enclosing area.
- **step-ah-lapse** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-lapse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-lapse): Adjoint positivity, weighted end barriers, compactness, and a low-lapse ratio minimum principle. -> Positive lapse floors, growth, end control, and compact regularity.
- **step-ah-graph** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-graph-estimates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-graph-estimates): Height maximum principles, localized tilt estimates, clipped-height energy tests, graph density, and end barriers. -> Finite slopes, positive graph scale, energy control, and end derivative decay.
- **step-ah-penalties** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-penalties) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-penalties): Test the positive conformal equation, analyze low-lapse sublevels, and enforce thresholds with scalar local supremum bounds. -> Small integrated penalty costs and enforced boundary and low-lapse targets.
- **step-ah-limit-mass** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-limit-mass) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-limit-mass): Compactness, end comparison, scalar linearization, and integration of the conserved current. -> Admissible limit metrics and a vanishing upper time-component mass cost.
- **step-ah-comparison-sphere** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-comparison-sphere) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-comparison-sphere): Solve an exterior auxiliary equation and use Green's identity with the mass budget. -> A uniformly bounded-area coordinate sphere for enclosure comparison.
- **step-ah-contact-selector** [claim](#stmt-lem-ah-contact-selector) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-ah-contact-selector): Compactify the limit family, prove upper semicontinuity of contact unions, and form a finite partition-of-unity majorant. -> Continuous allowable inner flux dominating all possible contact thresholds.
- **step-ah-finite-existence** [claim](#stmt-prop-ah-finite-existence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-ah-finite-existence): Construct a sequential compact elliptic map, use homotopy degree, and pass through expanding truncations. -> Smooth whole-exterior graph solution realizing the selector.
- **step-maximal-reduction** [claim](#stmt-thm-ah-reduction) / [proof](#pm-h-31): Exclude obstacle contact, form a free minimizing boundary, transfer area, and take successive error limits. -> The same continuous nondecreasing area bound for maximal data.
- **step-conformal-approximation** [claim](#stmt-prop-conformal-approximation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-conformal-approximation): Cut off the end, solve a small nonlinear conformal equation, derive an end expansion, and compare scalar flux tails. -> Strict-scalar conformal-end approximants preserving limiting mass and enclosing area.
- **step-electrostatic-stress** [claim](#stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress): Regularize the constitutive law, continue on truncations, prove gradient regularity, and derive stress and charge identities. -> Positive divergence-free stress and asymptotic charge saturation.
- **step-af-attachment** [claim](#stmt-prop-af-attachment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-af-attachment): Smooth stress with divergence control, match curvatures on a large sphere, and solve the quasi-spherical parabolic extension. -> Fixed synthetic compact data and a scalar-flat attachment with the cubic mass saving.
- **step-compact-lapse** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-lapse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-lapse): Capacitary flux bounds, reflected-sum Harnack estimates, lapse ratios, and gradient maximum contradictions. -> Uniform finite lapse and slope bounds independent of strengths and trace-target derivatives.
- **step-compact-penalties** [claim](#stmt-lem-compact-penalties) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-penalties): Positive conformal tests, low-lapse energy, zero-set source analysis, and finite-strength local threshold enforcement. -> Target conformal lower bounds, small penalty costs, and designated bad-volume control.
- **step-seam-holder** [claim](#stmt-lem-seam-holder) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-seam-holder): Green-weighted energy, frozen Newton-current cancellation, compatible-state compactness, and Campanato excess decay. -> Uniform seam Hölder bounds without trace-target derivatives or penalty-strength dependence.
- **step-transmission-schauder** [claim](#stmt-lem-transmission-schauder) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-transmission-schauder): Subtract scalar particular solutions, construct harmonic primitives, and use invertible positive harmonic combinations. -> Local mixed-order Schauder estimates and independent positive-ratio scalar estimates.
- **step-transmission-fredholm** [claim](#stmt-lem-transmission-fredholm) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-transmission-fredholm): Deform the principal background gradient, triangularize scalar blocks, and propagate index using finite-dimensional augmentation. -> Index zero for the linearized system and independent scalar density and adjoint problems.
- **step-transmission-existence** [claim](#stmt-prop-transmission-existence) / [proof](#pm-h-40): Bootstrap positive zeros, reduce a compact zero set to finite dimensions, and use regular-value continuation and endpoint parity. -> Positive piecewise smooth solutions on large truncations and a whole-exterior subsequential limit.
- **step-compact-construction** [claim](#stmt-prop-compact-solutions) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-compact-penalties-2): Combine finite penalty selection with independent transmission existence and integrate the matched current. -> Full attached graph comparison with scalar identities, area-loss control, and mass budget.
- **step-unsafe-blowup** [claim](#stmt-lem-unsafe-blowup) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-unsafe-blowup): Normalize unsafe points, control lapse before slopes, exclude nonzero limiting heights and seam limits, then apply gradient and truncated Harnack bounds. -> Radius-independent scaled metric comparability and seam escape.
- **step-corner-smoothing** [claim](#stmt-lem-corner-smoothing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-corner-smoothing): Mollify the Gaussian collar using the favorable curvature jump and solve a small coercive conformal correction. -> Smooth flat metric with controlled mass, strict boundary barrier, and scalar lower bounds.
- **step-free-enclosures** [claim](#stmt-lem-free-enclosure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-free-enclosure): Minimize perimeter with marked-ball obstacles, exclude contact using density and relative isoperimetry, and apply free-boundary regularity. -> Free outer-minimizing unsafe-region enclosure and largest cap-only enclosure.
- **step-af-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-af-comparison) / [proof](#pm-h-47): Assemble mass, omitted-collar, bad-volume, smoothing, and enclosure estimates in the prescribed order. -> Smooth flat comparison suitable separately for mass and finite-time area transfer.
- **step-time-symmetric-penrose** [claim](#stmt-thm-ts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-free-enclosure-2): Combine cubic attachment saving, flat mass comparison, cap-only area transfer, and the flat Penrose bound; then remove tolerances and approximation. -> The time-component inequality for the original Riemannian metric in its fixed chart.
- **step-maximal-penrose-sharpness** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-free-enclosure-3): Choose the original rest chart, apply the maximal reduction to the time-symmetric area function, and verify the Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter equality examples. -> Invariant-mass Penrose bound and sharp coefficient without a rigidity assertion.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-maximal-mass-area-bound**: The invariant mass satisfies the sharp Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter lower bound determined by the minimum enclosing area, under the stated maximal initial-data hypotheses.
- **invariant-time-component-without-causality**: The Riemannian lower bound controls the time component in every designated end chart without requiring a causal condition on the mass covector.
- **invariant-area-transfer-requires-weighted-volume**: Small weighted volume of the contracting region preserves the enclosing-area lower bound only together with the scalar lower bound, fixed capped topology, metric comparison, projection inequality, and minimizing-hull hypotheses.
- **invariant-distinct-enclosure-roles**: The cap-only enclosure supplies the area-transfer initial surface, while the enclosure containing the unsafe regions supplies the exterior with nonnegative scalar curvature for the asymptotically flat mass inequality.
- **invariant-sharpness-without-rigidity**: Positive-mass time-symmetric Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter exteriors bounded by their minimal horizons attain equality; this establishes sharpness without classifying all equality cases.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-nonmaximal-extension**: Apply the invariant-mass conclusion to initial data without maximality. -> The stated theorem does not establish the inequality for that larger class.
- **anti-raw-boundary-area**: Replace minimum enclosing area by the area of the original trapped boundary. -> The original boundary need not realize the infimum over admissible enclosing cuts.
- **anti-invariant-mass-without-future-timelikeness**: Use the invariant-mass theorem for a mass covector whose future-timelike condition has not been established. -> The rest-chart reduction used for the original covector is not justified.
- **anti-equality-classification**: Infer that attaining the mass bound characterizes Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter data. -> Examples attaining equality establish sharpness but do not establish the converse.
- **anti-pointwise-area-shortcut**: Deduce enclosing-area preservation solely from the graph metric increasing the base metric. -> The subsequent conformal factor can contract area, so graph comparison alone does not control the final enclosing-area infimum.
- **anti-penrose-on-unsafe-exterior**: Apply the asymptotically flat Penrose inequality directly to the exterior of the cap-only enclosure. -> That exterior may still contain regions where scalar curvature is negative.
- **anti-finite-sampling-as-global-proof**: Treat numerical agreement on sampled metrics or algebraic identities as certification of the global geometric theorem. -> Such checks do not establish existence, compactness, obstacle avoidance, or the limiting mass and area inequalities for the continuous geometric class.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The global mass-area result is not a finite constructive computation. The source proves existence through elliptic continuation, perimeter minimization, and subsequential limits on expanding truncations. The maximal construction explicitly states: “Expanding truncations have a subsequence converging to a solution smooth up to $S$ on the whole exterior.” The transmission construction likewise requires a subsequence converging on the full joined exterior. These existence and limiting arguments provide no finite decision procedure for the stated geometric class. Checking the displayed algebraic identities or the explicit sharpness family would cover only those subsidiary calculations and would not certify the global theorem.

          "exact_quote": "For every $M_e>0$ there is a weak solution $u$ of $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g E=0,\\qquad\n E=e(w)\\frac{\\nabla u}{w},\\quad w=|du|_g,\n \\qquad u|_S=-M_e,\\quad u\\longrightarrow0\\text{ at infinity},\n \\label{eq:stress-electrostatics}$$ where $E=0$ at $w=0$. The continuous symmetric tensor $$\\Pi=L(w)g-du\\otimes E^\\flat\n \\label{eq:stress-tensor}$$ is distributionally divergence free, is positive definite, and obeys $$(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\Pi)^2-2|\\Pi|_g^2=3.\n \\label{eq:stress-algebraic-identity}$$ There is a continuous nonnegative function $e_0$ on $\\mathbb S^2$ such that, uniformly in angle, $$r^2|E|_g\\longrightarrow e_0,\\qquad\n r^3\\big(\\Pi(\\nu,\\nu)-1\\big)\n       \\longrightarrow-\\tfrac12 e_0^{3/2}.\n \\label{eq:stress-end-asymptotics}$$ Here $\\nu$ points toward increasing $r$. The charge $$F_{M_e}=\\int_{r=R}g(E,\\nu)\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dA_g\n \\label{eq:stress-charge-definition}$$ is independent of large $R$, satisfies $F_{M_e}\\le\\int_{\\mathbb S^2}e_0\\,\\mathop{}\\!\\mathrm dA_\\sigma$, and $$\\liminf_{M_e\\to\\infty}F_{M_e}\\ge A_*.\n \\label{eq:stress-charge-saturation}$$",
          "source_object": "stmt-prop-electrostatic-stress"
        }
      ],

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-geometric-end-class** (hypothesis): The main inequality concerns smooth connected orientable complete exteriors with the prescribed spherical end and compact smooth boundary. Blocked use: ['Applying the conclusion to incomplete data, multiple ends, another dimension, or a different conformal infinity without a separate theorem.']
- **limit-maximality-and-rigidity-scope** (formal_scope): Nonmaximal initial data and equality rigidity are expressly outside the asserted scope. Blocked use: ['Extending the main theorem to nonmaximal data.', 'Classifying every equality case from the displayed sharpness examples.']
- **limit-weighted-tensor-decay** (hypothesis): The decay hypotheses concern background tensor norms and derivatives in uniform charts, with the stipulated decay exponent and regularity. Blocked use: ['Replacing weighted tensor decay by decay of Euclidean coordinate components.', 'Using a weaker decay regime without establishing the needed flux and elliptic conclusions.']
- **limit-energy-and-integrability** (hypothesis): The dominant energy condition and weighted matter integrability are hypotheses, rather than consequences of asymptotic decay alone. Blocked use: ['Invoking the maximal scalar-curvature sign or mass budget for matter violating the dominant energy condition.', 'Assuming weighted scalar integrability solely from pointwise decay.']
- **limit-original-mass-causal-character** (hypothesis): The invariant-mass conclusion requires the original finite mass covector to be future timelike. The Riemannian time-component theorem has a separate scope. Blocked use: ['Applying the invariant-mass theorem to null, spacelike, or past-directed covectors.', 'Adding a timelike-covector requirement to the separate Riemannian time-component theorem.']
- **limit-metric-charges-interpretation** (formal_scope): The spatial mass-covector entries are metric mass charges, not ADM momentum or angular momentum. Blocked use: ['Reading the invariant-mass inequality as a momentum or angular-momentum inequality.']
- **limit-future-boundary-orientation** (hypothesis): Future outer trapping uses the normal directed into the designated exterior on every boundary component. No inward null-expansion condition is assumed. Blocked use: ['Reversing the normal while retaining the same trapping inequality.', 'Replacing the future condition with an unrelated expansion sign.', 'Requiring an additional inward-expansion hypothesis as part of this theorem.']
- **limit-enclosing-area-intrinsic-boundary** (formal_scope): The bound uses minimum enclosing area with complete intrinsic competitor boundaries, including portions on the original boundary. Blocked use: ['Substituting the original boundary area without proving that it realizes the enclosing-area infimum.', 'Discarding boundary portions through a relative-perimeter convention.', 'Replacing the intrinsic boundary by an empty relative frontier.']
- **limit-cut-enclosure-converse** (hypothesis): The converse from an enclosure to an admissible cut requires smooth free boundary and connected exterior; identifying its own enclosing-area minimum additionally uses outward minimization. Blocked use: ['Converting an arbitrary finite-perimeter enclosure into an admissible smooth cut.', 'Identifying a local perimeter stationary surface with the required global enclosing-area minimum.']
- **limit-scalar-inputs-versus-transmission** (formal_scope): The local scalar elliptic estimates do not themselves establish a general nonlinear transmission theorem. Blocked use: ['Applying scalar reflection or Schauder estimates to the coupled seam problem before proving its coefficient and interface hypotheses.']
- **limit-finite-state-energy-estimates** (hypothesis): The differential energy and frozen-current estimates require finite slope and positive bounded lapse and scale ranges. Their constants may depend on those ranges. Blocked use: ['Treating the energy estimate as uniform through lapse degeneration or unbounded slopes.', "Transferring the maximum estimate's lack of a lapse floor to every subsequent energy estimate."]
- **limit-static-graph-not-spacetime-evolution** (formal_scope): The shared graph identities are identities on a Riemannian base and do not construct a spacetime satisfying field equations. Blocked use: ['Interpreting the auxiliary graph height as physical time evolution.', 'Identifying the later synthetic tensor with the original initial-data second fundamental form.']
- **limit-area-transfer-full-criterion** (hypothesis): Small contraction volume preserves enclosing area only together with the proposition's topology, scalar lower bound, minimizing-hull, metric-comparison, and projection hypotheses. Blocked use: ['Deducing area preservation solely from the graph metric dominating the base metric.', 'Using an unweighted bad-volume estimate where the hyperbolic application requires the prescribed weight.', 'Omitting the seam measure condition in the piecewise projection argument.']
- **limit-flow-area-window-and-null-area** (edge_case): The curvature control is an almost-everywhere statement up to a prescribed area ceiling. The zero-area case is handled without invoking a positive-area transfer argument. Blocked use: ['Replacing the finite relative-area argument by an unproved limit of hyperbolic Hawking mass at infinity.', 'Claiming the weak-flow curvature bound at every time.', 'Applying a positive-area contradiction interval when the original enclosing area vanishes.']
- **limit-ah-parameter-order-and-exhaustion** (approximation): The maximal deformation takes the outer exhaustion limit with internal parameters fixed and selects finite penalty strengths only after the preceding parameters. Blocked use: ['Taking an uncontrolled simultaneous limit of truncation radius, height, lapse cutoff, and penalty strength.', 'Assuming that a finite strength works uniformly before the required cutoff and state bounds are fixed.']
- **limit-contact-selector-not-computable-detector** (nonconstructive): The continuous inner-flux rule is obtained from a compact family of limit fields and all possible perimeter-minimizer contacts; its existence is not a finite contact-detection algorithm. Blocked use: ['Replacing the all-contact majorant with a test against one chosen minimizer.', 'Claiming a terminating implementation of the selector from continuity alone.']
- **limit-elliptic-existence-not-finite-certification** (nonconstructive): The whole-exterior deformation relies on degree continuation and subsequences of expanding truncations. A finite decision procedure for the global geometric theorem is ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Treating sampled algebraic identities as certification of the global mass-area theorem.', 'Inferring solver convergence, uniqueness, termination, or computational complexity from existence.']
- **limit-conformal-approximation-mass-control** (approximation): The preliminary approximation preserves the limiting mass through a separate weighted scalar-flux argument; local metric convergence alone is insufficient. Blocked use: ['Inferring mass convergence from local metric convergence or a decay weight below the required mass order.', 'Demanding uniform later construction estimates across all approximating metrics when the proof fixes an approximant first.']
- **limit-electrostatic-charge-only-lower-limit** (approximation): Charge saturation is a lower-limit inequality in potential height, not an asserted equality at finite height. The weak stress is smoothed after choosing the attachment sphere. Blocked use: ['Replacing the charge lower-limit statement by exact finite-height saturation.', 'Using the continuous electrostatic stress as an already smooth synthetic tensor.', 'Choosing tensor smoothing uniformly as the attachment sphere tends to infinity without an additional estimate.']
- **limit-fixed-attachment-and-transmission-range** (hypothesis): The compact graph stage fixes smooth synthetic data and the attachment before varying deformation parameters; its transmission estimates operate on compact positive finite-state ranges. Blocked use: ['Changing the attachment geometry during the compact continuation while claiming the same constants.', 'Extending seam regularity uniformly through vanishing lapse or unbounded slope.', 'Discarding the strict seam mean-curvature gap or current matching.']
- **limit-compact-penalties-and-omitted-collars** (approximation): The designated bad-volume estimate does not by itself cover the omitted collars. The full estimate additionally controls the exterior collar and the shrinking inner collar in the prescribed order. Blocked use: ['Applying area transfer using only the designated-region estimate.', 'Choosing graph height before resolving the dependence on the volume penalty and omitted exterior collar.']
- **limit-unsafe-scale-quantifier-order** (hypothesis): The unsafe-scale metric comparison has a common constant chosen before the fixed scaled radius, while the height threshold may depend on that radius. Blocked use: ['Allowing the metric-comparison constant to grow with the obstacle radius in the perimeter contradiction.', 'Requiring one height threshold to work simultaneously at all scaled radii.']
- **limit-smoothing-at-fixed-solution** (approximation): Corner smoothing and conformal correction are chosen separately after fixing each comparison solution. Scalar nonnegativity is retained only off the unsafe set. Blocked use: ['Assuming a uniform smoothing tolerance across the entire family of comparison solutions.', 'Claiming globally nonnegative scalar curvature for the smoothed metric before enclosing the unsafe set.']
- **limit-distinct-enclosures-for-mass-and-area** (hypothesis): The mass theorem uses the free enclosure hiding unsafe regions; finite-time area transfer starts from the largest cap-only minimizing enclosure. Blocked use: ['Applying the asymptotically flat Penrose theorem to a cap-only exterior that still contains unsafe scalar curvature.', 'Assuming a topology bound for the unsafe-region enclosure is supplied by the cap-only flow argument.', 'Dropping smoothness, outer minimization, nonnegative exterior scalar curvature, or asymptotic decay when invoking the flat theorem.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove the sharp Penrose inequality for three-dimensional maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data with spherical conformal infinity. Under the dominant energy condition, the stated decay and integrability assumptions, and a future-timelike mass covector, the invariant mass is bounded below by the Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter mass associated with the minimum enclosing area of a weakly future outer-trapped boundary. The boundary may be disconnected, and no restriction is imposed on the compact topology.

<a id="sec:hypotheses"></a>
### Introduction and statement of the result

The Penrose inequality relates the mass of an initial-data set to the area needed to enclose a trapped region. Penrose’s original argument (Penrose 1973) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Penrose1973](#ref-Penrose1973)] connects such a bound with gravitational collapse and the expected behavior of black holes. In the asymptotically flat Riemannian case, Huisken and Ilmanen proved the connected-horizon inequality by weak inverse mean curvature flow (Huisken and Ilmanen 2001) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[HI2001](#ref-HI2001)], and Bray proved the inequality for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon (Bray 2001) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Bray2001](#ref-Bray2001)]. Bray and Lee extended the Riemannian result to dimensions below eight (Bray and Lee 2009) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)].

For negative cosmological constant the natural comparison metric is Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter. Its horizon of area $4\pi a^2$ has mass $(a+a^3)/2$ when the cosmological constant is $-3$. The additional cubic term is accompanied by a different asymptotic mass: the four fluxes at spherical conformal infinity form a Lorentz covector (Chruściel and Herzlich 2003) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[CH2003](#ref-CH2003)]. For asymptotically hyperbolic graphs, Dahl, Gicquaud, and Sakovich established mass identities and Penrose-type bounds (Dahl, Gicquaud, and Sakovich 2013) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[DGS2013](#ref-DGS2013)]; de Lima and Girão proved the sharp bound for a class of balanced graphs whose horizons are star-shaped and mean convex in the reference slice (Lima and Girão 2016) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[deLimaGirao2016](#ref-deLimaGirao2016)]. Directly passing to infinity along inverse mean curvature flow has a distinct obstruction in this setting (Neves 2010) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Neves2010](#ref-Neves2010)].

Here we prove the global maximal asymptotically hyperbolic Penrose inequality in the class specified below. Thus the corresponding maximal formulation of the Penrose conjecture is resolved positively, with arbitrary compact topology and without an outermostness assumption on the original boundary. The area in the statement is the minimum *enclosing* area, not necessarily the area of that boundary. The proof does not require a spacetime development or an additional null-expansion condition. We make no assertion about nonmaximal initial data or equality rigidity.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Geometry, decay, and mass

<a id="eq:background"></a>
Let $(\Omega,g)$ be a smooth connected orientable three-manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$. The metric space obtained by including $S$ is complete. There is one end, with coordinates $(r,\omega)\in(r_0,\infty)\times\mathbb S^2$ outside a compact region. Write $$\label{eq:background}
 b=\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm dr^2}{1+r^2}+r^2\sigma,
 \qquad \eta=\operatorname{arsinh}r,
 \qquad V_0=\sqrt{1+r^2},\qquad V_i=r\omega_i\quad(1\le i\le3),$$ where $\sigma$ is the unit round metric and $\omega_i$ are the coordinate functions of the unit sphere. The Laplacian is $\Delta=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\nabla$; mean curvature is the sum of the principal curvatures.

Fix $0<\alpha<1$ and $3/2<\tau<3$. On the end, a tensor belongs to $C^{k,\alpha}_\tau$ if its $b$-covariant derivatives through order $k$ are $O(e^{-\tau\eta})$, and its order-$k$ local Hölder seminorms on uniform $b$-unit coordinate balls have the same weight. Equivalently, the $C^{k,\alpha}$ norms of its components in uniform background charts, multiplied by $e^{\tau\eta}$ at the chart centers, are bounded. This convention is a tensor-norm convention. It does not mean Euclidean coordinate-component decay. On compact subsets, including the finite boundary, all fields below are smooth.

<a id="eq:decay"></a>
<a id="eq:ah-mass"></a>
<a id="eq:mass-integrand"></a>
<a id="eq:invariant-mass"></a>
Let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor on $\Omega$, smooth up to $S$, and assume $$\label{eq:decay}
 g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_\tau,
 \qquad K\in C^{1,\alpha}_\tau.$$ For $e=g-b$, define the mass fluxes in the chosen chart by $$\begin{aligned}
\label{eq:ah-mass}
 p_\mu(g)&=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty}
       \int_{\{r=R\}}\mathbb U(V_\mu,e)(\nu_b)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_b,
       &&0\le\mu\le3,\\
 \mathbb U(V,e)&=V(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_b e-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_b e)
              +(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_b e)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV-e(\nabla_b V,\cdot).
              \label{eq:mass-integrand}
\end{aligned}$$ Here $(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_b e)_i=\nabla_b^j e_{ji}$, and $\nu_b$ points toward increasing $r$. Every operator and measure in this definition uses $b$. We require the four limits to exist and be finite. When the covector is future timelike, its invariant mass is $$\label{eq:invariant-mass}
 m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g)=\sqrt{p_0(g)^2-p_1(g)^2-p_2(g)^2-p_3(g)^2},
 \qquad p_0(g)>\sqrt{p_1(g)^2+p_2(g)^2+p_3(g)^2}.$$ The spatial entries in this covector are metric mass charges; they are not ADM momentum or angular momentum.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Constraints, boundary, and enclosing area

<a id="eq:constraints"></a>
<a id="eq:dec-integrability"></a>
We use units $G=c=1$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda=-3$. Maximality and the noncosmological constraint densities are $$\label{eq:constraints}
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0,
 \qquad 16\pi\mu=R_g+6-|K|_g^2,
 \qquad 8\pi J_i=\nabla_g^jK_{ij}.$$ Assume the dominant energy condition and weighted integrability $$\label{eq:dec-integrability}
 \mu\ge|J|_g,
 \qquad \int_{\mathrm{end}}V_0
       \bigl(\mu+|J|_g+|K|_g^2\bigr)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty.$$ In particular $R_g+6\ge0$ and its $V_0$-weighted integral is finite.

<a id="eq:future-trapping"></a>
On each component of $S$, choose the unit normal $\nu$ pointing into $\Omega$, toward the designated exterior. Set $$\label{eq:future-trapping}
 H=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu,
 \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=(g^{ij}-\nu^i\nu^j)K_{ij},
 \qquad \theta_+=H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK.$$ We assume only $\theta_+\le0$ on every component, with this same future orientation. For comparison with a spacetime convention, the sign is $K(X,Y)=\overline g(\overline\nabla_Xn_{\mathrm{future}},Y)$. There is no assumption on the inward null expansion.

<a id="stmt-def-minimum-area"></a>
<div id="def:minimum-area" class="definition">

**Definition 1** (Minimum enclosing area). An admissible end-side domain is a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega$, closed as a subset of $\Omega$, such that $$\operatorname{int}D\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \{r>R\}\subset D\quad\hbox{for some }R.$$ Its entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\partial D$ must be compact, smooth, embedded, and two-sided, with any portions coinciding with $S$ included. Define <a id="eq:minimum-area"></a>$$\label{eq:minimum-area}
 A_{\min}(S;g)=\inf_D\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\partial D).$$ In particular $D=\Omega$ is admissible and contributes $\partial D=S$. An empty relative frontier is not an admissible replacement for this intrinsic boundary.

</div>

Neither the number nor the genus of the boundary components is restricted. No trapping condition is imposed on the competitors in Definition <a href="#def:minimum-area" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:minimum-area">1</a>.

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:main-inequality"></a>
**Theorem 2** (Global maximal AH Penrose inequality). *Under <a href="#eq:decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:decay">[eq:decay]</a>–<a href="#eq:future-trapping" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:future-trapping">[eq:future-trapping]</a>, the completeness, one-end, and smoothness assumptions above, and the future-timelike condition <a href="#eq:invariant-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:invariant-mass">[eq:invariant-mass]</a>, one has $$\label{eq:main-inequality}
 m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g)\ge\frac12\bigl(r_A+r_A^3\bigr),
 \qquad r_A=\sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}}.$$ The coefficient is sharp: equality holds for every positive-mass time-symmetric Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter exterior bounded by its minimal horizon.*

</div>

The proof establishes a time-component statement for Riemannian data which is useful independently and which does not require a causal condition on their mass covector.

<a id="stmt-thm-ts"></a>
<div id="thm:ts" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:ts-inequality"></a>
**Theorem 3** (Time-symmetric time-component inequality). *Let $(\Omega,g)$ have the smoothness, topology, completeness, and end structure above. Suppose $g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_\tau$, $3/2<\tau<3$, the four fluxes <a href="#eq:ah-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-mass">[eq:ah-mass]</a> are finite, and $$R_g\ge-6,\qquad H_g(S)\le0,
 \qquad \int_{\mathrm{end}}V_0(R_g+6)\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty.$$ In every such fixed end chart, $$\label{eq:ts-inequality}
 p_0(g)\ge\frac12(a+a^3),
 \qquad a=\sqrt{A_{\min}(S;g)/(4\pi)}.$$*

</div>

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### Structure and new ingredients

The first deformation solves a finite-height graph problem together with a positive lapse and a conformal factor. It changes maximal data into Riemannian AH data with scalar curvature at least $-6$ and a free minimal boundary. Its mass cost tends to zero. The conformal factor can contract area, so pointwise comparison alone is insufficient. A volume penalty and a finite-time weak-flow argument recover the enclosing-area comparison. A continuous choice of inner flux, based on all possible perimeter-minimizer contact sets, removes contact with the original weakly trapped boundary.

For Theorem <a href="#thm:ts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ts">3</a>, a nonlinear electrostatic potential produces a divergence-free stress. Its algebraic constraint encodes the cubic term $a^3/2$ in the mass budget of an AF attachment. A second graph construction on a compact interior joined to that attachment yields an AF comparison exterior to which the ordinary Riemannian Penrose inequality applies. We prove the coupled transmission estimates and continuation needed for this construction. Where a trace cutoff can spoil the scalar-curvature sign, blowup gives uniformly controlled metric neighborhoods; additional obstacles then put these regions strictly inside a free minimizing enclosure.

The area comparison uses weak inverse mean curvature flow only over a fixed interval of relative areas. Its curvature estimate depends on a scalar lower bound and fixed topology, and accommodates disconnected leaves. It therefore has a role different from taking an asymptotic limit of hyperbolic Hawking mass.

The numerical argument can be seen before entering these constructions. In the positive-area time-symmetric case, fix a metric after the preliminary approximation and write $A_{\min}(S;g)=4\pi a^2$. Let $E_0$ denote the comparison enclosure of the auxiliary caps alone and $E$ the enclosure that also contains the regions where scalar curvature may be negative. Given small positive tolerances $\varepsilon_m,\varepsilon_A$, the attachment and comparison constructions, followed by area transfer, give $$\begin{aligned}
 m_o&\le p_0(g)-a^3/2+\varepsilon_m,
 &m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h')&\le m_o+\varepsilon_m,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{h'}(\partial E)&\ge\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{h'}(\partial E_0)
                    \ge(1-\varepsilon_A)4\pi a^2.
 \end{aligned}$$ (Propositions <a href="#prop:af-attachment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-attachment">30</a>, <a href="#prop:af-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-comparison">38</a>, and <a href="#prop:area-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:area-transfer">19</a>). The AF Penrose inequality applies to the exterior of $E$ and yields $$p_0(g)\ge \frac{a^3}{2}
       +\frac a2\sqrt{1-\varepsilon_A}-2\varepsilon_m.$$ Thus the attachment supplies the cubic term and the AF inequality the linear term. The errors tend to zero through successive finite choices; no convergence of the comparison metrics is required. Theorem <a href="#thm:ah-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ah-reduction">20</a> then transfers the time-symmetric bound to maximal data. The original mass covector is put in a rest chart before any deformation, so its time component is the invariant mass.

Sections <a href="#sec:graph-calculus" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:graph-calculus">3</a> and <a href="#sec:area-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:area-transfer">4</a> develop the shared identities and area comparison. Section <a href="#sec:maximal-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:maximal-reduction">5</a> reduces Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a> to Theorem <a href="#thm:ts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ts">3</a>. Sections <a href="#sec:stress-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:stress-extension">6</a>–<a href="#sec:scalar-error" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scalar-error">9</a> construct the AF comparison for the latter. Section <a href="#sec:completion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:completion">10</a> assembles the inequalities and checks sharpness.

<a id="sec:preliminaries"></a>
### Preliminaries

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### Compact cores and auxiliary caps

<a id="stmt-lem-compact-core"></a>
<div id="lem:compact-core" class="lemma">

**Lemma 4**. *The sufficiently large coordinate spheres bound connected compact truncations of $\Omega$. Each component of $S$ can be capped on its other side to produce a smooth complete connected one-ended manifold $X$ without boundary, with the orientation extending that of $\Omega$. Let $O$ denote the compact cap set, including its boundary. For competitors containing $O$, perimeter depends only on the metric on $\Omega$ and its boundary trace.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-compact-core"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-compact-core</summary>

*Proof.* The end metric is uniformly comparable to $b$ sufficiently far out. Radial infinity escapes compact subsets: otherwise a sequence tending to radial infinity would accumulate in a compact coordinate neighborhood, while pairwise disjoint background balls of a fixed small radius about a subsequence would have uniformly positive metric volumes and lie in a fixed compact neighborhood. This is impossible. A large coordinate sphere separates the product end from an inner side. If the latter were noncompact, a smooth compact exhaustion would yield an end separated from the given product end. One may choose this exhaustion with finitely many complement components at each stage, since its smooth compact frontier has finitely many components. Nested extraction then contradicts the one-end assumption. The inner side is therefore compact. Paths between its points can be pushed back across the product end, so the truncations can be taken connected.

Every component of $S$ is a closed orientable surface and bounds a handlebody. Orient each handlebody and glue by a map reversing the induced boundary orientations. The collars then extend the orientation of $\Omega$ across each seam. Extend the metric smoothly across $S$. The added region is compact; completeness at infinity is unchanged. For a set containing $O$ up to a null set, its characteristic function is constant almost everywhere in the cap interiors. Its perimeter therefore uses no metric values there. ◻

</details>

We use the ordinary perimeter of a finite-perimeter set in the capped manifold. In particular it is not a relative perimeter that discards the original boundary.

<a id="stmt-lem-cut-enclosure"></a>
<div id="lem:cut-enclosure" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5**. *Every admissible cut from Definition <a href="#def:minimum-area" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:minimum-area">1</a> determines a precompact finite-perimeter enclosure of $O$ whose perimeter is at most the area of that cut. Conversely, a precompact enclosure of $O$ with smooth free boundary in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$ and connected exterior gives an admissible cut with the same area. If this enclosure is outward minimizing, its boundary realizes the minimum enclosing area of its own closed exterior.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-cut-enclosure"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-cut-enclosure</summary>

*Proof.* For an admissible $D$, complement its manifold interior in $X$. The result contains $O$ and is precompact because $D$ contains the whole sufficiently distant end. Local boundary coordinates show that its perimeter is bounded by the entire intrinsic area of $\partial D$, including any portions on $S$. This also follows by smoothing corners and passing to the perimeter lower limit. For the converse, take the closed exterior of the smooth enclosure. It is connected, has the required end, and has precisely the stated intrinsic boundary. Any admissible cut of this new exterior, complemented in $X$, encloses the original enclosure; outward minimization gives the final claim. ◻

</details>

The compactness, lower semicontinuity, coarea, slicing, reduced-boundary structure, and union/intersection inequalities for finite-perimeter sets will be used below. These are local facts and hold in smooth Riemannian coordinate charts; see Maggi (2012, vol. 135, chaps. 12–18) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[Maggi2012](#ref-Maggi2012)]. They also give compactness and lower semicontinuity for a uniformly convergent family of uniformly positive continuous metrics on a fixed compact set, by comparison with smooth metrics. A free locally perimeter-minimizing boundary is smooth in ambient dimension three; one may use the smooth-ambient regularity theorem in Simon (2014, chap. 7, Section 5, Theorem 5.8) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[Simon2014](#ref-Simon2014)], followed by elliptic bootstrapping. We invoke this regularity only after excluding contact with every obstacle and outer truncation.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Mass covariance and small metric changes

<a id="stmt-prop-mass-covariance"></a>
<div id="prop:mass-covariance" class="proposition">

**Proposition 6**. *Suppose $g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_\tau$, $\tau>3/2$, and $\int V_0|R_g+6|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty$ on the end. The fluxes <a href="#eq:ah-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-mass">[eq:ah-mass]</a> transform as a Lorentz covector under hyperbolic isometries of the asymptotic chart. Such chart changes preserve the weighted decay and integrability hypotheses used here. Consequently a future-timelike original covector admits a chart with $p_0=m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}$ and $p_1=p_2=p_3=0$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-mass-covariance"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-mass-covariance</summary>

*Proof.* The potentials in <a href="#eq:background" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:background">[eq:background]</a> are the ambient coordinate functions of the future unit hyperboloid. Hyperbolic isometries act on their span by Lorentz transformations. The flux integrand is tensorial in $b$, linear in $V$, and natural under these isometries. It remains to justify replacing the transformed integration surfaces by the original large coordinate spheres. The static identity $\nabla_b^2V=Vb$ gives $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_b\mathbb U(V,e)=V\,D R_b(e).$$ The difference between $D R_b(e)$ and $R_g+6$ is bounded by a constant times $$|e|_b^2+|\nabla_be|_b^2+|e|_b|\nabla_b^2e|_b.$$ Its $V_0$-weighted integral over $r>D$ is $O(D^{3-2\tau})$, since $\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_b$ is comparable to $r\mathop{}\!\mathrm dr\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_\sigma$. Also $|V_i|\le V_0$. Thus the divergence is absolutely integrable on the end for each potential. The divergence theorem on regions between the two families of spheres makes their flux difference tend to zero. This is the covariance mechanism of Chruściel and Herzlich (2003, Proposition 2.2, Theorem 2.3, and Section 3) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[CH2003](#ref-CH2003)] in the normalization <a href="#eq:ah-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-mass">[eq:ah-mass]</a>.

A fixed hyperbolic isometry changes distance from the chosen origin by a bounded amount. The exponential weights and $V_0$ are therefore comparable before and after the change, and uniform background balls are carried to uniform background balls. The rest-chart assertion is the elementary Lorentz normal form of a future-timelike covector. ◻

</details>

The boundary sign and the enclosing-area definition are intrinsic. We will apply Proposition <a href="#prop:mass-covariance" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:mass-covariance">6</a> to the original data before constructing any comparison metric. No assertion that intermediate covectors remain timelike is required.

If $(1-\varepsilon)g\le\widetilde g\le(1+\varepsilon)g$ as quadratic forms, then for every two-surface its area changes by factors between $1-\varepsilon$ and $1+\varepsilon$. Taking infima over the same admissible domains gives the same comparison for $A_{\min}$. This observation will be used when passing through the preliminary conformal approximation and the later corner smoothing.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### The AF comparison theorem

<a id="eq:adm-mass"></a>
For an AF metric $h$ in a Euclidean end chart $y$, our normalization is $$\label{eq:adm-mass}
 m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h)=\frac1{16\pi}\lim_{R\to\infty}
 \int_{|y|=R}(\partial_jh_{ij}-\partial_ih_{jj})
                  n^i\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA_{\mathrm{Eucl}}.$$

<a id="stmt-thm-af-penrose"></a>
<div id="thm:af-penrose" class="theorem">

**Theorem 7** (AF Riemannian Penrose inequality). *Let $(Y,h)$ be a complete connected one-ended three-dimensional AF manifold with smooth compact outer-minimizing minimal boundary. Assume $R_h\ge0$, $h-\delta=O_2(|y|^{-\beta})$ for some $\beta>1/2$, and $R_h=O(|y|^{-q})$ for some $q>3$. If the total boundary area is $A$, then <a id="eq:af-penrose"></a>$$\label{eq:af-penrose}
 m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h)\ge\sqrt{A/(16\pi)}.$$ Disconnected boundary is allowed.*

</div>

This is the dimension-three case of the published Bray and Lee (2009, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)]; its asymptotic definition is on page 82 and its boundary convention on page 83. Only the inequality is used. The smoothness, scalar sign, and outer-minimization required here will be established for the AF comparison exterior, rather than assumed for either original AH metric.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
#### Local scalar elliptic estimates

We specify the standard local analytic inputs, separating them from the coupled transmission estimates proved in Section <a href="#sec:transmission-analysis" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:transmission-analysis">8</a>.

<a id="stmt-prop-elliptic-inputs"></a>
<div id="prop:elliptic-inputs" class="proposition">

**Proposition 8** (Scalar local estimates). *On fixed coordinate balls in dimension three the following estimates hold, with constants depending on the indicated ellipticity, coefficient, and geometry bounds.*

1.  *Bounded measurable uniformly elliptic divergence matrices admit local subsolution bounds, weak Harnack estimates for nonnegative supersolutions, and inhomogeneous Harnack and Hölder estimates for nonnegative solutions. Bounded divergence drifts multiplying the unknown, vector forcing in $L^q$, $q>3$, and scalar forcing in $L^p$, $p>3/2$, are permitted in the corresponding estimates.*

2.  *For Laplace equations with uniformly positive Lipschitz metric coefficients in interior or flattened smooth boundary charts, divergence forcing in $L^q$ gives local $W^{1,q}$ estimates. Scalar forcing in $L^2$ can be included for $3<q<6$. The same statements hold with local zero Dirichlet data or natural Neumann data, with the divergence forcing included in the conormal current. A boundary datum in $L^{p_1}$, $p_1>2$, permits a choice $3<q<3p_1/2$ sufficiently close to $3$.*

3.  *Smooth-coefficient scalar Dirichlet and conormal problems have the usual Schauder estimates, including divergence-form $C^{1,\gamma}$ estimates when the uniformly elliptic coefficients and vector forcing are $C^\gamma$, with boundary data of the corresponding regularity. These estimates are used only after their coefficient hypotheses have been obtained.*

4.  *For a bounded measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix $a$ on a ball, its positive Dirichlet Green kernel is bounded above by $C|z-z'|^{-1}$, and below by $c|z-z'|^{-1}$ when the pole and the nearby evaluation point lie in a fixed smaller ball.*

</div>

The local boundedness, Harnack, and Hölder estimates are the scalar divergence theory of Serrin (1964) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Serrin1964](#ref-Serrin1964)] and Gilbarg and Trudinger (2001, chap. 8) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[GT2001](#ref-GT2001)]. The Laplace divergence estimates are the local Calderón–Zygmund estimates, with smooth-boundary localization; see Stein (1970; Gilbarg and Trudinger 2001) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Stein1970](#ref-Stein1970), [GT2001](#ref-GT2001)]. For natural Neumann data, an explicit estimate is given by Choi and Kim (2013, Appendix, proof of Lemma 6.1, (6.2), p. 19 of arXiv v3) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[ChoiKim2013](#ref-ChoiKim2013)] on bounded $C^1$ localizations. Our Lipschitz metric coefficients are VMO. A cutoff retains the full conormal current and the larger-patch $W^{1,2}$ norm. In dimension three the scalar and boundary forcing exponents are $3q/(q+3)$ and $2q/3$, respectively, so approximation permits $3<q<\min\{6,3p_1/2\}$ for the data in part (ii). For the boundary exponent in part (ii), the trace embedding of $W^{1,q'}$ into $L^{2q/(2q-3)}$ on a two-dimensional face allows pairing with $L^{p_1}$ whenever $q<3p_1/2$. Scalar $L^2$ forcing belongs locally to $W^{-1,q}$ when $q<6$. Part (iv) is the local Green comparison of Littman, Stampacchia, and Weinberger (1963, Theorem 7.1 and the discussion on pp. 66–67) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[LSW1963](#ref-LSW1963)].

Natural homogeneous flux permits even reflection in a flattened boundary chart, with the full current reflected. Smooth prescribed flux errors can be placed in a bounded smooth vector field. Fermi-coordinate metric matrices reflected at a smooth face are Lipschitz. Constant Dirichlet data for a scalar height permit odd reflection after subtraction of that constant. We spell out each reflection where it is needed; none of these scalar statements is a general nonlinear transmission theorem.

For the electrostatic equation we also use an exact degenerate gradient regularity statement. Suppose $$A(z,0)=0,\qquad
 \lambda|\xi|I\le A_\xi(z,\xi)\le C|\xi|I,
 \qquad
 |A(z,\xi)-A(z',\xi)|\le C|z-z'|\,|\xi|^2,$$ with symmetric $A_\xi$, continuous dependence, and smooth dependence on $\xi\ne0$. Then a bounded weak $W^{1,3}$ solution of $\partial_iA^i(z,\mathop{}\!\mathrm du)=0$ is locally $C^{1,\gamma}$ for some $\gamma>0$, with uniform estimates from the structural constants and a local energy bound. Indeed $A_\xi(z,0)=0$ extends continuously, and integration along a radial segment gives $|A(z,\xi)|\le C|\xi|^2$. The assumptions of Araújo and Zhang (2020, Theorem 1.1, (1.5)–(1.8)) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[AraujoZhang2020](#ref-AraujoZhang2020)] therefore hold with $n=p=3$, zero forcing in $L^\infty$, and spatial Hölder exponent $\sigma=1/2$. We use only an exponent $0<\gamma<\min\{\alpha_m,1/4\}$, where $\alpha_m>0$ is a constant-coefficient gradient exponent for the same structural constants. No optimal exponent or endpoint estimate is required. If these inequalities initially hold only on a known bounded gradient range, the constitutive law must first be extended with the same structure; that extension is constructed in Section <a href="#sec:stress-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:stress-extension">6</a>.

All global invertibility, weighted end estimates, seam regularity, continuation, and uniform large-parameter conclusions used later are proved below. The local estimates in this subsection supply only their explicitly stated scalar ingredients.

<a id="sec:graph-calculus"></a>
### Static graph identities and differential estimates

This Section proves the differential identities used in both constructions. They are identities on a Riemannian base; no spacetime satisfying field equations is assumed. In particular, the reference tensor in this Section may be either the given maximal tensor or the synthetic tensor constructed later.

The curvature, current, and boundary identities give the scalar, mass, and boundary inequalities in both deformations. The maximum estimate controls finite slopes without differentiating the trace cutoff; the energy and Newton-current estimates supply the seam-continuity argument in Section <a href="#sec:transmission-analysis" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:transmission-analysis">8</a>.

<a id="eq:calculus-volume-inverse"></a>
Let $(U,g)$ be a smooth three-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Unless a metric is displayed, covariant derivatives, norms, contractions, volume forms, and divergences in this Section use $g$. For a symmetric covariant tensor $C$, the notation $C p$ means the vector obtained by contracting with $p$ and raising the remaining index with $g$. For a positive smooth function $N$ and a smooth function $f$, define $s>0$ and $p$ by <a id="eq:calculus-constitutive"></a>$$p=s^2\nabla f,\qquad s^2+|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df|^2s^4=N^2,
 \qquad v=\frac pN,\qquad W=\frac Ns,
 \qquad \bar g=g+s^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm df\otimes\mathop{}\!\mathrm df.
 \label{eq:calculus-constitutive}$$ The positive root is unique, and it depends smoothly on $(N,\mathop{}\!\mathrm df)$, including at $\mathop{}\!\mathrm df=0$, because <a id="eq:calculus-positive-root"></a>$$s^2=\frac{2N^2}{1+\sqrt{1+4N^2|\mathop{}\!\mathrm df|^2}}.
 \label{eq:calculus-positive-root}$$ We use $d=s/N=\sqrt{1-|v|^2}$ for a scalar in $(0,1]$; differentials are written $\mathop{}\!\mathrm d$. Direct rank-one inversion and the determinant formula give $$\bar g^{-1}=g^{-1}-v\otimes v,\qquad
 \mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\bar g}=W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g.
 \label{eq:calculus-volume-inverse}$$ For a further positive function $w$ put <a id="eq:calculus-conformal-definitions"></a>$$x=sw,\qquad h=x\bar g,\qquad A=Ns\bar g^{-1},
 \qquad \pi=N^{-1}\operatorname{sym}\nabla p^\flat,
 \label{eq:calculus-conformal-definitions}$$ where $\operatorname{sym}$ is the half-sum. The tensor $\pi$ throughout this Section is the graph second fundamental form, not the electrostatic stress introduced in Section <a href="#sec:stress-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:stress-extension">6</a>. The elementary identities <a id="eq:calculus-energy-algebra"></a>$$p\cdot\mathop{}\!\mathrm df=W^2-1,\qquad
 A(\mathop{}\!\mathrm df,\mathop{}\!\mathrm df)=W-W^{-1}\le p\cdot\mathop{}\!\mathrm df,
 \qquad 0<A\le N^2g^{-1}
 \label{eq:calculus-energy-algebra}$$ will also be used in the penalty estimates.

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Curvature and the conserved current

<a id="stmt-lem-graph-curvature"></a>
<div id="lem:graph-curvature" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:calculus-lapse-differential"></a>
<a id="eq:calculus-static-curvature"></a>
<a id="eq:calculus-completed-curvature"></a>
**Lemma 9** (Static graph curvature). *Suppose that $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p=TN$, where $T$ is a smooth scalar function. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\pi=T$ and $$\begin{aligned}
 \bar\nabla\log s&=\nabla\log N-\pi(v),
 \label{eq:calculus-lapse-differential}\\
 R_{\bar g}
 &=R_g+T^2-|\pi|^2-2(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\pi-\mathop{}\!\mathrm dT)\cdot v.
 \label{eq:calculus-static-curvature}
\end{aligned}$$ More generally, let $\mathcal K$ be any smooth symmetric covariant tensor, and define <a id="eq:calculus-trace-definitions"></a>$$\kappa=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\mathcal K,\qquad
 \ell=T-\kappa,\qquad \lambda=\pi-\mathcal K,
 \qquad C=\lambda-\ell g,
 \label{eq:calculus-trace-definitions}$$ and <a id="eq:calculus-dominant-expression"></a>$$\mathscr D(v)=R_g+\kappa^2-|\mathcal K|^2
       -2(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\mathcal K-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\kappa)\cdot v.
 \label{eq:calculus-dominant-expression}$$ Then $$R_{\bar g}=\mathscr D(v)+|\lambda|^2-\ell^2
                   -\frac2N\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp).
 \label{eq:calculus-completed-curvature}$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-graph-curvature"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-graph-curvature</summary>

*Proof.* The trace assertion follows immediately from the definition of $\pi$. To prove the first identity without any geometric interpretation, set $a=\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log s$. Since $p^\flat=s^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm df$, $$\nabla_i p_j=N\pi_{ij}+a_i p_j-a_j p_i.$$ Differentiating $s^2=N^2-|p|^2$ and substituting this formula gives $$N^2a_i-(a\cdot p)p_i=N\nabla_iN-N\pi_{ij}p^j.$$ Division by $N^2$ and Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-volume-inverse" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-volume-inverse">[eq:calculus-volume-inverse]</a> give Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-lapse-differential" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-lapse-differential">[eq:calculus-lapse-differential]</a>, as an equality of vectors.

For the curvature identity consider, solely for this computation, the Lorentzian metric $$\widetilde g=-s^2\mathop{}\!\mathrm dt^2+\bar g$$ on $\mathbb R\times U$. The graph $t=f$ has induced metric $g$. If $X^\mathrm{tan}=X+\mathop{}\!\mathrm df(X)\partial_t$, its future unit normal is $n=(\partial_t+p^\mathrm{tan})/N$. Thus $\partial_t=Nn-p^\mathrm{tan}$. The tangential part of the Killing equation for $\partial_t$ is $N\widetilde g(\widetilde\nabla_{X^\mathrm{tan}}n,Y^\mathrm{tan})
=\operatorname{sym}\nabla p^\flat(X,Y)$. Its second fundamental form, with the sign convention specified after <a href="#eq:future-trapping" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:future-trapping">[eq:future-trapping]</a>, is therefore $\pi$.

Write $\widetilde G$ for the Einstein tensor and $n_0=s^{-1}\partial_t$ for the normal to a static slice. The contracted Gauss and Codazzi identities with timelike unit normal and second form $\widetilde g(\widetilde\nabla n,\cdot)$ read $$2\widetilde G(n,n)=R_g+T^2-|\pi|^2,
 \qquad
 \widetilde G(n,X^\mathrm{tan})
       =(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\pi-\mathop{}\!\mathrm dT)(X).$$ The static slices have zero second form. Applying these same contractions to a static slice gives $\widetilde G(n_0,n_0)=R_{\bar g}/2$ and $\widetilde G(n_0,X)=0$ for spatial $X$. The static time component of $n$ is $N/s$, whereas that of $\partial_t/N$ is $s/N$. Consequently $$\frac12R_{\bar g}
 =\widetilde G(n,\partial_t/N)
 =\widetilde G(n,n)-\widetilde G(n,v^\mathrm{tan}),$$ which proves Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-static-curvature" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-static-curvature">[eq:calculus-static-curvature]</a> with the claimed sign of the momentum term.

For completeness, the completion of the square uses symmetry to give $$\frac1N\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp)
 =(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\lambda-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\ell)\cdot v
                         +\lambda:\pi-\ell T.$$ Also $2\ell T-\ell^2=T^2-\kappa^2$ and $|\lambda|^2-2\lambda:\pi=|\mathcal K|^2-|\pi|^2$. Substituting these two equalities in the right side of Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-completed-curvature" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-completed-curvature">[eq:calculus-completed-curvature]</a> recovers Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-static-curvature" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-static-curvature">[eq:calculus-static-curvature]</a> term by term. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-lem-graph-current"></a>
<div id="lem:graph-current" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:calculus-general-x"></a>
<a id="eq:calculus-general-conformal"></a>
**Lemma 10** (Graph current and conformal curvature). *Under the hypotheses and notation of Lemma <a href="#lem:graph-curvature" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:graph-curvature">9</a>, set <a id="eq:calculus-general-system"></a>$$B=\nabla N-(\mathcal K+\ell g)p,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B=\Phi,\qquad -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)=\Psi,
 \qquad Q=B+A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw.
 \label{eq:calculus-general-system}$$ Then <a id="eq:calculus-general-current"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 Q&=N\bar\nabla x+xCp-(x-1)B,\notag\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g Q&=\Phi-\Psi,
 \label{eq:calculus-general-current}\\
 N\Delta_{\bar g}x+x\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp)&=x\Phi-\Psi,
 \label{eq:calculus-general-x}\\
 xR_h&=\mathscr D(v)+|\lambda|^2-\ell^2
       -\frac{2\Phi}{N}+\frac{2\Psi}{Nx}
       +\frac32|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log x|_{\bar g}^2.
 \label{eq:calculus-general-conformal}
\end{aligned}$$ In particular, the following two specializations hold.*

**The maximal AH system.* If $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK=0$ and <a id="eq:calculus-ah-system"></a>$$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p=0,\quad B=\nabla N-Kp,\quad
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B=3N+\Sigma,\quad
 -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)=3N+\Sigma x+P,
 \label{eq:calculus-ah-system}$$ then, writing $D=R_g+6-|K|^2-2\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gK\cdot v$, one has <a id="eq:calculus-ah-current"></a><a id="eq:calculus-ah-x"></a><a id="eq:calculus-ah-curvature"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 Q&=N\bar\nabla x+x(\pi-K)p-(x-1)B,\notag\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g Q&=-(x-1)\Sigma-P,
 \label{eq:calculus-ah-current}\\
 \left(\Delta_{\bar g}-3+
          N^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g((\pi-K)p)\right)x&=-3-P/N,
 \label{eq:calculus-ah-x}\\
 x^2(R_h+6)
 &=x\bigl(D+|\pi-K|^2\bigr)
   +\frac{3}{2x}|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx|_{\bar g}^2
   +6(x-1)^2+\frac{2P}{N}.
 \label{eq:calculus-ah-curvature}
\end{aligned}$$ For the constraint densities in <a href="#eq:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:constraints">[eq:constraints]</a>, $D=16\pi(\mu-J\cdot v)\ge0$ under the dominant energy condition.*

<a id="eq:calculus-compact-current"></a>
**The compact trace system.* Let $0\le u_*\le1$ be constant and take $\mathcal K=u_*K$, $\kappa=u_*\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$, $\ell=T-\kappa$. If <a id="eq:calculus-compact-system"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g p&=TN,&
 B&=\nabla N-(u_*K+\ell g)p,\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g B&=\Sigma_++\Sigma_-,&
 -\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)&=\Sigma_+x+P,
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:calculus-compact-system}$$ then <a id="eq:calculus-compact-curvature"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 Q&=N\bar\nabla x+x(\lambda-\ell g)p-(x-1)B,\notag\\
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gQ&=-(x-1)\Sigma_+-P+\Sigma_-,
 \label{eq:calculus-compact-current}\\
 xR_h&=\mathscr D(v)+|\lambda|^2-\ell^2
             -\frac{2\Sigma_-}{N}+\frac{2P}{Nx}
             +\frac32|\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log x|_{\bar g}^2.
 \label{eq:calculus-compact-curvature}
\end{aligned}$$ Here $\lambda=\pi-u_*K$. At $u_*=1$ this is the scalar identity for the synthetic data. It also holds on the outer region with $p=T=K=\ell=0$, $\Sigma_-=0$, and $\mathscr D=R_{g_o}$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-graph-current"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-graph-current</summary>

*Proof.* Since $w=x/s$, Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-lapse-differential" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-lapse-differential">[eq:calculus-lapse-differential]</a> gives $$A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw=N\bar\nabla x-Nx\bar\nabla\log s
        =N\bar\nabla x-x\nabla N+x\pi p.$$ Adding $B$ proves the first formula for $Q$. Its divergence from the defining equations is $\Phi-\Psi$. To compute the divergence of its other expression, Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-volume-inverse" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-volume-inverse">[eq:calculus-volume-inverse]</a> gives $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(N\bar\nabla x)
 &=N\Delta_{\bar g}x
       +N\bar g^{-1}(\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\log s,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx)\\
 &=N\Delta_{\bar g}x+(\nabla N-\pi p)\cdot\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx.
\end{aligned}$$ The derivative-of-$x$ terms in $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(xCp+(1-x)B)$ are $(Cp-B)\cdot\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx=(\pi p-\nabla N)\cdot\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx$. They cancel exactly, leaving $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gQ=N\Delta_{\bar g}x+x\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp)+(1-x)\Phi.$$ This proves Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-general-x" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-general-x">[eq:calculus-general-x]</a>. In dimension three the conformal change $h=x\bar g$ has scalar curvature $$xR_h=R_{\bar g}-2x^{-1}\Delta_{\bar g}x
                     +\frac32x^{-2}|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dx|_{\bar g}^2.$$ Substitution of Equations <a href="#eq:calculus-completed-curvature" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-completed-curvature">[eq:calculus-completed-curvature]</a> and <a href="#eq:calculus-general-x" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-general-x">[eq:calculus-general-x]</a> cancels the two occurrences of $2N^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g(Cp)$ and proves Equation <a href="#eq:calculus-general-conformal" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:calculus-general-conformal">[eq:calculus-general-conformal]</a>. The two stated systems now follow by substituting their values of $T,\mathcal K,\Phi,\Psi$. In the AH case, the nondifferential cosmological terms after multiplication by $x$ are $6x^2-12x+6=6(x-1)^2$. Finally, $|v|<1$ and the constraint definitions give the asserted sign of $D$. ◻

</details>

For later use, the divergence theorem makes these current formulas into exact finite-domain flux budgets. Let $S$ be the inner boundary, with normal pointing into the domain, let $S_R$ have the outward normal, and suppose $B_n=-b_S$ and $(A\mathop{}\!\mathrm dw)_n=0$ on $S$. The scalar $b_S$ is a boundary datum, unrelated to the hyperbolic reference metric $b$. In the compact construction assume also that the two currents have matching normal flux at their common face, measured toward the end. Then <a id="eq:calculus-flux-budget"></a>$$-\int_{S_R}Q_n\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\int_S b_S\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA+
    \int_{U_R}\bigl[(x-1)\Sigma+P\bigr]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV,
       &\text{for \eqref{eq:calculus-ah-system}},\\[3pt]
 \displaystyle\int_S b_S\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dA+
    \int_{U_R}\bigl[(x-1)\Sigma_++P-\Sigma_-\bigr]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV,
       &\text{for \eqref{eq:calculus-compact-system}}.
 \end{cases}
