Adjoin that collar to a purported minimizer. Gauss–Green on the added portion bounds the newly exposed leaf area minus the removed perimeter by the integral of this negative divergence. The added volume is positive for every sufficiently small width at a contact point; otherwise that point would not be in the perimeter support. Slicing allows an almost every width for which all perimeter formulas hold. The resulting strict decrease contradicts minimality. Adjoining a collar is permitted whether or not marked balls are present.

The perimeter support is thus separated from both obstacles and the outer constraint. It is locally perimeter minimizing in a smooth three-manifold. Interior codimension-one minimizing boundary regularity gives a smooth compact embedded minimal surface. Take its open set representative for $E$. Filling any bounded open exterior component would strictly reduce perimeter, so its open exterior is connected. Since every precompact enlargement is an admissible competitor, $E$ is outward minimizing. Its boundary is disjoint from every marked ball, so the unsafe set lies in its interior. The metric on its closed exterior has nonnegative scalar curvature, and its completeness and unique AF end follow from smoothness of compact truncations and the AF estimates.

Now minimize with obstacle $O$ alone. The same compactness, outer barriers, and strict inner mean-curvature barrier give a smooth free minimal boundary and a connected open exterior. Every component of this open minimizer meets $O$, because an open component disjoint from $O$ can be removed, strictly reducing perimeter. Choose a minimizer of maximal volume within the fixed truncation. It is a largest minimizer modulo null sets: the perimeter submodularity inequality implies that the union and intersection of any two minimizers are minimizers, and maximal volume forces the union to agree with this one. Denote its open representative by $E_0$. Any proper precompact enlargement of equal perimeter would also be a minimizer and would contradict maximal volume. The outer barriers allow this reasoning without the truncation. Thus $E_0$ is strictly outward minimizing. Its boundary avoids $S$, so $O\Subset E_0$. Finally $E$ is itself an admissible enclosure of $O$, proving <a href="#eq:unsafe-two-perimeters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-two-perimeters">[eq:unsafe-two-perimeters]</a>. ◻

</details>

No bound on the number or topology of components created by the marked balls has been used. In particular the subsequent area transfer starts from $E_0$, not from a topological assertion about $E$. The hypotheses for the AF Riemannian Penrose theorem are satisfied by the closed exterior of $E$: it is smooth, complete and one-ended, its scalar curvature is nonnegative and decays as $O(|x'|^{-2-2\beta})$, with $2+2\beta>3$, its metric decay has exponent $\beta>1/2$, and its entire possibly disconnected minimal boundary is outer minimizing. The boundary version of Bray and Lee (2009, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)] therefore gives <a id="eq:unsafe-af-penrose"></a>$$m_{h'}\ge\sqrt{\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{Per}}_{h'}(E)}{16\pi}}.
 \label{eq:unsafe-af-penrose}$$

<a id="pm-h-47"></a>
#### Bad volume and completion of the comparison

<a id="eq:unsafe-total-bad-volume"></a>
We finish the proof of Proposition <a href="#prop:af-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-comparison">38</a> by checking the uniform quantitative inputs for Proposition <a href="#prop:area-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:area-transfer">19</a>. The exterior capacity comparison in Section <a href="#sec:compact-construction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compact-construction">7</a> gives $x\ge1-\psi_\infty$, so for fixed $\delta>0$ the set $\{x<1-\delta\}$ does not reach beyond a fixed outer sphere. On the designated region, <a href="#eq:compact-bad-volume" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-bad-volume">[eq:compact-bad-volume]</a> gives $\int_{\{x<1-\delta\}}W\le C/L$. The omitted exterior collar has $W=1$, so its contribution is bounded by its base volume. The omitted inner collar has base volume $O(M^{-4})$. Cauchy–Schwarz and <a href="#eq:compact-height-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-height-energy">[eq:compact-height-energy]</a> together with <a href="#eq:compact-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:compact-bounds">[eq:compact-bounds]</a> therefore give $$\int_{\{x<1-\delta\}}W\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_{\rm base}
 \le \frac CL+\mathop{\mathrm{Vol}}_{g_o}(\text{omitted exterior collar})
       +C(L)M^{-1}.
 \label{eq:unsafe-total-bad-volume}$$ The coefficient in $C/L$ is independent of $L$. The other constants may depend on the earlier collar choice and on $L$, which is harmless: first make the exterior collar thin and $L$ large, then let $M$ be large.

Choose $b_*,\delta_0$ small enough in <a href="#eq:unsafe-mass-limsup" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-mass-limsup">[eq:unsafe-mass-limsup]</a> for the prescribed mass tolerance. For the prescribed $\delta$ and volume tolerance choose the collar and $L$ as just described. Fix the common comparator bound, choose $R_*$ in Lemma <a href="#lem:free-enclosure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:free-enclosure">41</a>, and then choose $M$ large enough for that lemma, the scalar lower bound, the mass costs, and <a href="#eq:unsafe-total-bad-volume" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-total-bad-volume">[eq:unsafe-total-bad-volume]</a>. The subsequent small lapse cutoff and finite strengths are those of Proposition <a href="#prop:compact-solutions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:compact-solutions">31</a>; all uniform estimates above hold for those choices. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:corner-smoothing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:corner-smoothing">40</a> with mass and metric errors small enough for the remaining tolerances. These choices prove <a href="#eq:unsafe-comparison-output" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-comparison-output">[eq:unsafe-comparison-output]</a>–<a href="#eq:unsafe-bad-volume-output" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-bad-volume-output">[eq:unsafe-bad-volume-output]</a>.

The caps may be fixed once as topological handlebodies, regardless of all metric parameters. The topology entering the area-transfer argument is consequently the fixed finite topology of $X\setminus\operatorname{int}O$. Positive-time flow levels outside $E_0$ are allowed to enter the unsafe region: the uniform lower scalar bound there is precisely the input supplied by <a href="#eq:unsafe-comparison-output" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:unsafe-comparison-output">[eq:unsafe-comparison-output]</a>. The mass theorem is applied to the unmodified smooth exterior of $E$, whereas the small initial mean-curvature change used solely for the flow is covered by Proposition <a href="#prop:area-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:area-transfer">19</a>. This completes the AF comparison construction.

<a id="sec:completion"></a>
### Completion of the proof

<a id="pm-h-49"></a>
#### The time-symmetric inequality

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-free-enclosure-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-free-enclosure</summary>

*Proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:ts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ts">3</a>.* The approximation of Proposition <a href="#prop:conformal-approximation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:conformal-approximation">28</a> preserves $H(S)\le0$, converges uniformly in metric comparison, and preserves the limiting time component. The comparison of enclosing areas in Section <a href="#sec:preliminaries" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminaries">2</a> therefore allows us first to assume that $R_g+6>0$ and that the end has the smooth conformal form used in Section <a href="#sec:stress-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:stress-extension">6</a>. Fix this approximated metric for the constructions that follow, and put $$A_*=A_{\min}(S;g),\qquad a=\sqrt{A_*/(4\pi)}.$$

<a id="eq:completion-attachment-budget"></a>
Given an arbitrarily small mass tolerance $\varepsilon_m>0$, Proposition <a href="#prop:af-attachment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-attachment">30</a> produces a fixed compact inner piece, a smooth synthetic tensor on it, and a scalar-flat AF attachment with mass $m_o$ satisfying $$\label{eq:completion-attachment-budget}
 m_o\le p_0(g)-\frac{a^3}{2}+\varepsilon_m.$$ The electrostatic height, attachment radius, and smoothing tolerances used to obtain this inequality have already been fixed. They are independent of the large graph height in the next construction.

Apply Proposition <a href="#prop:compact-solutions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:compact-solutions">31</a> and the comparison construction of Proposition <a href="#prop:af-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:af-comparison">38</a>. Their parameters are chosen in the proved order: the small inner flux and scalar cutoff costs first, then a desired relative-area tolerance $0<\varepsilon_A<1$, a sufficiently small contraction threshold, a thin omitted exterior collar, and a sufficiently large fixed volume penalty; next the graph height is taken large, and finally the lapse clipping, finite penalty strengths, and corner-smoothing tolerances are chosen. The costs can be made small enough that the resulting smooth AF comparison metric satisfies <a id="eq:completion-comparison-budget"></a>$$\label{eq:completion-comparison-budget}
 m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h')\le m_o+\varepsilon_m.$$

<a id="eq:completion-area"></a>
Let $E$ be its minimizing enclosure containing the caps and the unsafe-region obstacles. Its free boundary is smooth, compact, minimal, and outer minimizing. The exterior is complete and has $R_{h'}\ge0$, the AF decay required in Theorem <a href="#thm:af-penrose" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:af-penrose">7</a>, and one end. Let $E_0$ instead be a largest perimeter-minimizing enclosure of the caps alone. Then <a id="eq:completion-enclosure-order"></a>$$\label{eq:completion-enclosure-order}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{h'}(\partial E)\ge\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{h'}(\partial E_0).$$ The exterior of $E_0$ has a scalar lower bound independent of the large graph height, even where it meets the unsafe region. The bad-volume estimates from Sections <a href="#sec:compact-construction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:compact-construction">7</a> and <a href="#sec:scalar-error" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scalar-error">9</a>, together with the projection along the AF attachment, satisfy Proposition <a href="#prop:area-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:area-transfer">19</a>. Consequently, when $A_*>0$, the parameters above can be chosen so that $$\label{eq:completion-area}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{h'}(\partial E_0)\ge(1-\varepsilon_A)A_*.$$ The small initial conformal change used only for the flow fixes this initial area. It is not made in applying the mass theorem.

Theorem <a href="#thm:af-penrose" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:af-penrose">7</a> applies to the exterior of $E$, not the possibly unsafe exterior of $E_0$. Equations <a href="#eq:completion-attachment-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:completion-attachment-budget">[eq:completion-attachment-budget]</a>–<a href="#eq:completion-area" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:completion-area">[eq:completion-area]</a> give $$\begin{aligned}
 p_0(g)
 &\ge \frac{a^3}{2}+m_o-\varepsilon_m\\
 &\ge \frac{a^3}{2}+m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AF}}}(h')-2\varepsilon_m\\
 &\ge \frac{a^3}{2}+\frac a2\sqrt{1-\varepsilon_A}
                         -2\varepsilon_m.
\end{aligned}$$ Let the two tolerances tend to zero, making fresh choices of the finite parameters as necessary. If $A_*=0$, the same construction and the nonnegativity consequence of Theorem <a href="#thm:af-penrose" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:af-penrose">7</a> give $p_0(g)\ge-2\varepsilon_m$ without the area step. Thus <a href="#eq:ts-inequality" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ts-inequality">[eq:ts-inequality]</a> holds for every fixed approximated metric. Passing back through the preliminary approximation proves it for the original metric. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-50"></a>
#### Maximal data and invariant mass

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-free-enclosure-3"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-free-enclosure</summary>

*Proof of the inequality in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a>.* The maximal constraint and <a href="#eq:dec-integrability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:dec-integrability">[eq:dec-integrability]</a> imply $$\int_{\mathrm{end}} V_0|R_g+6|\mathop{}\!\mathrm dV_g<\infty.$$ Use Proposition <a href="#prop:mass-covariance" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:mass-covariance">6</a> to choose a rest chart for the original covector. All hypotheses remain valid in that chart and $p_0(g)=m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g)$.

Define $$F(A)=\frac12\left(\sqrt{\frac A{4\pi}}
                       +\left(\frac A{4\pi}\right)^{3/2}\right).$$ This function is continuous, nonnegative, and nondecreasing on $[0,\infty)$. Theorem <a href="#thm:ts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ts">3</a> supplies the time-symmetric input of Theorem <a href="#thm:ah-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ah-reduction">20</a>, including comparison metrics whose covectors are not timelike. The reduction therefore gives $$p_0(g)\ge F\bigl(A_{\min}(S;g)\bigr).$$ Since the chart was fixed before any construction, this is precisely <a href="#eq:main-inequality" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:main-inequality">[eq:main-inequality]</a>. The one-sided time-component budgets suffice; there is no further assertion about the spatial components of intermediate comparison metrics. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-51"></a>
#### Sharpness

Let $m>0$, and let $a$ be the positive solution of $a+a^3=2m$. The Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter metric is <a id="eq:sads-metric"></a>$$\label{eq:sads-metric}
 g_m=\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm dr^2}{1+r^2-2m/r}+r^2\sigma,
 \qquad r\ge a,\qquad K=0.$$ To include its boundary smoothly, use proper distance $s$ from $r=a$. Then $$g_m=\mathop{}\!\mathrm ds^2+r(s)^2\sigma,
 \quad r(0)=a,\quad r'(0)=0,
 \quad (r')^2=1+r^2-2m/r.$$ The simple positive radial derivative of the expression on the right at $a$ gives a smooth even solution $r(s)$ near zero, increasing for $s>0$. Hence the horizon is a smooth minimal boundary and the exterior is complete with that boundary included. Since $r''=r+m/r^2$, the warped-product formula gives $$R_{g_m}=-\frac{4r''}{r}
             +\frac{2(1-(r')^2)}{r^2}=-6.$$ The constraints are vacuum, the metric error and its required tensor derivatives are $O(r^{-3})$, and the weighted matter integral vanishes.

For completeness the mass normalization can be checked directly. In the background distance coordinate, write $g_m-b=\zeta\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\eta^2$, where $$\zeta=\frac{2m}{r(1+r^2-2m/r)}.$$ The radial component of $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_b e-\mathop{}\!\mathrm d\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_be$ is $2\coth\eta\,\zeta$, and the other two terms of <a href="#eq:mass-integrand" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:mass-integrand">[eq:mass-integrand]</a> cancel for $V_0$. The normalized sphere flux therefore tends to $$m\frac{1+r^2}{1+r^2-2m/r}\longrightarrow m.$$ Rotational symmetry makes the three spatial fluxes zero, so $m_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{AH}}}(g_m)=m$.

Radial projection onto the horizon has two-area Jacobian at most one, since $r\ge a$. Every radial ray meets the entire intrinsic boundary of any admissible end-side domain: either it enters that domain across its boundary, or its initial point already lies on the counted boundary at $S$. Thus projection of the cut covers the horizon. The area formula gives $\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_{g_m}(\partial D)\ge4\pi a^2$. The horizon itself is an admissible competitor, and hence $A_{\min}(S;g_m)=4\pi a^2$. Equation $2m=a+a^3$ proves equality in <a href="#eq:main-inequality" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:main-inequality">[eq:main-inequality]</a> and completes Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">2</a>.
